learn.hook: The beach is full of shells! How can we count them fast?
points: Put things in groups of the same size.
Count group by group to find how many in all.
Groups of 2, 5 or 10 are easy to count.
Grouping does not change the total. It only makes counting easy.

example.q: Aisha has 3 groups of 5 shells. How many shells?

learn.reallife: Mummy counts socks in pairs. The fruit seller counts bananas in bunches.

games.title: True or false?
items: Putting things in groups changes how many there are.
The total stays the same. Groups only make counting easy.

quiz.q: Riya puts shells in 4 groups of 5. How many shells?
quiz.explain: Count by 5s for 4 groups: 5, 10, 15, 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 5 instead of counting 4 groups of 5

quiz.q: Arjun makes 3 groups of 10 pebbles. How many pebbles?
quiz.explain: Count by 10s for 3 groups: 10, 20, 30.
quiz.mistake: Writes 1 and 3 together or adds 3 and 10

quiz.q: There are 6 pairs of slippers on the sand. How many slippers?
quiz.explain: A pair is 2. Count by 2s six times: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12.
quiz.mistake: Counts pairs instead of slippers

quiz.q: Meena counts starfish: 10, 20, 30, 40. How many groups of 10 is that?
quiz.explain: She said 4 numbers: 10, 20, 30, 40. So there are 4 groups of 10.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total instead of the number of groups

quiz.q: Why do we count shells in groups?
quiz.explain: Groups help us count fast with fewer mistakes. The number of shells stays the same.
steps: Groups do not add or take away shells.
So counting in groups is quicker and easier.
Answer: It is quicker and easier
quiz.mistake: Thinks grouping changes the total

quiz.q: Kabir sees 2 groups of 5 crabs and 3 more crabs. How many crabs?
quiz.explain: 2 groups of 5 is 10. Then 3 more: 11, 12, 13.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 3 extra crabs

teach.ask: Gappu: There are so many shells! How can I count them quickly?
teach.praise: Wow! Make equal groups and count group by group. So fast!
teach.nudge: Should I put them in groups? Must every group be the same size?

revise.summary: We put things in groups of the same size and count group by group to find how many in all. Grouping does not change the total; it only makes counting easy.
focus: Count groups of 2, 5 or 10 by saying 5, 10, 15 ... or 10, 20, 30.
Find the total of some groups plus a few extra things.
Tell the number of groups apart from the total.
remember: Groups of 2, 5 or 10 are easy to count.
Grouping does not change the total.
traps: Don't add 4 and 5 for 4 groups of 5. Count 5, 10, 15, 20.
Don't forget the extra things left outside the groups.
Don't count the pairs when you need the number of slippers.

learn.hook: The beach is busy! Boats, coconuts and children everywhere. Let us count them all.
points: Count one kind of thing at a time and write its total.
Tick each thing as you count, so you do not count it twice.
Bananas come in bunches. Count the bunches, then add the loose ones.
The same total can come from different groups: 10 groups of 5 and 5 groups of 10 both make 50.
Many things are packed in tens, like pencils, toffees and biscuits.

example.q: A fruit seller has 2 bunches of 10 bananas and 4 loose bananas. How many bananas?

learn.reallife: A shopkeeper sells pencils in boxes of 10 and toffees in packets of 10.

games.title: True or false?
items: 10 groups of 5 and 5 groups of 10 both make 50.
Five tens make 50. Ten fives also make 50.
Pencils are often sold in boxes of 10.
A box of 10 is easy to count and sell.
Ticking each boat helps us not count it twice.
A tick shows the boat is already counted.
2 bunches of 10 and 2 loose bananas make 40.
Counting in groups gives a different total than counting one by one.
Both ways give the same total. Groups are just faster.

quiz.q: Count the coconuts: 🥥🥥🥥🥥🥥🥥🥥. How many coconuts?
quiz.explain: Touch and count each one: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.
steps: Touch each coconut as you count.
quiz.mistake: Skips or counts a coconut twice

quiz.q: A seller has 3 bunches of 10 bananas and 5 loose bananas. How many bananas?
quiz.explain: 3 bunches are 10, 20, 30. Then 5 loose: 31, 32, 33, 34, 35.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the loose bananas or swaps tens and ones

quiz.q: Which makes the same total as 5 groups of 10?
quiz.explain: 5 groups of 10 is 50. Count 10 groups of 5: 5, 10, 15 ... 50. Same total!
quiz.mistake: Thinks a different grouping must give a different total

quiz.q: Which of these is often sold in boxes of 10?
quiz.explain: Pencils are small, so shops pack them in tens. We buy one bicycle or one bag at a time.
steps: Small things are packed in boxes of 10.
Pencils are small. We buy one bicycle, tank or bag.
So pencils come in boxes of 10.
quiz.mistake: Does not link small things with packs of ten

quiz.q: Gita counts children: 🧒🧒🧒🧒🧒 🧒🧒🧒🧒🧒 🧒🧒. How many children?
quiz.explain: Two groups of 5 make 10. Then 2 more make 12.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the full groups

quiz.q: Mohan has 6 bunches of 5 bananas. Lata has 3 bunches of 10. Who has more?
quiz.mistake: Thinks more bunches always means more bananas

teach.ask: Gappu: The fruit seller has bunches and some loose bananas. How do I count them all?
teach.praise: Yes! Count the bunches in tens, then add the loose ones. Easy!
teach.nudge: Should I count the bunches first? What about the loose ones?

revise.summary: In a busy picture, count one kind of thing at a time and tick each one. For bananas, count the bunches first, then add the loose ones.
focus: Tick each thing as you count so you do not count it twice.
Count bunches or packs of 10, then count on the loose ones.
See that different groups can give the same total.
remember: 10 groups of 5 and 5 groups of 10 both make 50.
Many things are packed in tens, like pencils, toffees and biscuits.
traps: Don't forget the loose bananas after counting the bunches.
Don't think more bunches always means more bananas.
Don't skip a thing or count it twice.

learn.hook: Hop like a frog! Skip one number each time: 2, 4, 6, 8!
points: Counting by 2s means adding 2 each time.
2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 ... we jump over one number.
We count eyes, ears, shoes and wheels of a cycle by 2s.
Counting by 2s is faster than counting one by one.

example.q: There are 5 pairs of shoes outside the beach hut. How many shoes?

learn.reallife: We count shoes at the temple door or wheels of cycles by 2s.

games.title: Frog hops
games.prompt: Put them in order, counting by 2s

quiz.q: Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, ___. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Add 2 each time. 8 + 2 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Counts on by 1 instead of 2

quiz.q: Joseph counts slippers by 2s: 10, 12, 14, ___?
quiz.mistake: Counts on by 1, or jumps by 4

quiz.q: 5 children sit on the sand. Count their eyes by 2s. How many eyes?
quiz.explain: Each child has 2 eyes. 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
quiz.mistake: Counts children, not eyes

quiz.q: Which number is missing? 20, 22, ___, 26
quiz.mistake: Counts on by 1

quiz.q: Riya counts by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 9. Which number is wrong?
quiz.explain: After 6 comes 6 + 2 = 8, not 9. So 9 is wrong.
quiz.mistake: Does not check that each jump is 2

quiz.q: There are 4 cycles. Each cycle has 2 wheels. How many wheels?
quiz.explain: Count by 2s for 4 cycles: 2, 4, 6, 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 2 instead of counting 2 for each cycle

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I count by 2s? Show me!
teach.praise: Yes! Add 2 every time: 2, 4, 6, 8. Hop hop!
teach.nudge: How many do I add each time I hop?

revise.summary: Counting by 2s means adding 2 each time: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. It is faster than counting one by one.
focus: Say the next number when counting by 2s.
Find a missing or wrong number in a 2s pattern.
Count eyes, shoes and cycle wheels by 2s.
remember: Counting by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 ... add 2 each time.
traps: Don't count on by 1 when you are counting by 2s.
Don't count the children when the question asks for eyes.
Check that each jump is 2.

learn.hook: One hand has 5 fingers. Two hands have 10. Let's count big numbers fast!
points: Counting by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 ... add 5 each time.
Numbers we say when counting by 5s end in 5 or 0.
Counting by 10s: 10, 20, 30 ... add 10 each time.
Numbers we say when counting by 10s end in 0.

example.q: Harpreet has 4 bags. Each bag has 10 sea shells. How many shells?

learn.reallife: We count ₹10 coins or fingers on many hands by 10s and 5s.

quiz.explain: Add 5 each time. 15 + 5 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Counts on by 1 instead of 5

quiz.explain: Add 10 each time. 30 + 10 = 40.
quiz.mistake: Counts on by 1 instead of 10

quiz.q: Aisha has 6 coins of ₹10. How much money is that?
quiz.explain: Count by 10s six times: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 and 10 instead of counting by 10s

quiz.q: 4 friends hold up one hand each. Count the fingers by 5s.
quiz.explain: One hand has 5 fingers. 5, 10, 15, 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 5, or counts one hand too many

quiz.q: Which number is missing? 35, 40, ___, 50
quiz.mistake: Counts on by 1, or skips one number too many

quiz.q: Count back by 10s: 90, 80, 70, ___
quiz.explain: Going back, take away 10 each time. 70 − 10 = 60.
steps: Counting back by 10: take away 10 each time.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 1 instead of 10

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I count by 10s? And by 5s?
teach.praise: Super! 10, 20, 30 and 5, 10, 15. Big jumps!
teach.nudge: How many do I add each time when I count by 5s? And by 10s?

revise.summary: Counting by 5s adds 5 each time and counting by 10s adds 10 each time. We use them to count fingers and ₹10 coins fast.
focus: Say the next number when counting by 5s or 10s.
Find a missing number in a 5s or 10s pattern.
Count back by 10s by taking away 10 each time.
remember: Counting by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 ... numbers end in 5 or 0.
Counting by 10s: 10, 20, 30 ... numbers end in 0.
traps: Don't count on by 1 instead of 5 or 10.
Don't add 6 and 10 for six ₹10 coins. Count 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60.
When counting back by 10s, don't take away just 1.

learn.hook: Ammu packs 10 chikoos in each tray. Can you count the trays to find all the chikoos?
points: One full tray holds 10 chikoos.
Count trays in tens: 1 tray is 10, 2 trays are 20, 8 trays are 80.
25 chikoos are 2 full trays and 5 loose chikoos.
Full trays tell the tens. Loose chikoos tell the ones.

example.q: How many full trays and loose chikoos make 43?

learn.reallife: Eggs and fruits at the market are often kept in trays.

quiz.q: Ammu has 8 full trays. Each tray holds 10 chikoos. How many chikoos?
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 and 10 instead of counting 8 tens

quiz.q: Ravi has 25 chikoos. How many full trays of 10 can he fill?
quiz.explain: 25 is 20 and 5. 20 fills 2 trays. 5 are not enough for another tray.
quiz.mistake: Reads the ones digit as trays

quiz.q: 25 chikoos fill 2 trays. How many chikoos are left loose?
quiz.explain: 2 trays hold 20. 25 take away 20 leaves 5 loose.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up trays and loose chikoos

quiz.q: Which of these shows 58 chikoos?
quiz.explain: In 58, 5 is tens and 8 is ones. So 5 full trays and 8 loose.
steps: 8 ones = 8 loose. Answer: 5 trays and 8 loose
quiz.mistake: Swaps the tens and ones digits

quiz.q: Raj sees 3 trays and 5 loose chikoos. What number is this?
quiz.explain: 3 trays are 30. 5 loose make 35.
quiz.mistake: Writes the loose number first

quiz.q: Meera has 4 full trays and 3 loose chikoos. Sita has 43 chikoos. Who has more?
quiz.explain: 4 trays and 3 loose make 40 + 3 = 43. Sita also has 43.
quiz.mistake: Does not turn trays into tens

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 35 chikoos. How many trays of 10 can I fill?
teach.praise: Yes! 3 full trays and 5 loose. You are a super packer!
teach.nudge: How many tens are in 35? How many are left over?

revise.summary: One full tray holds 10 chikoos. Full trays tell the tens and loose chikoos tell the ones, so 25 is 2 full trays and 5 loose.
focus: Count trays in tens: 8 trays are 80.
Split a number into full trays and loose chikoos.
Turn trays and loose chikoos back into a number.
remember: One full tray holds 10 chikoos.
Full trays tell the tens. Loose chikoos tell the ones.
traps: Don't swap the tens and ones: 58 is 5 trays and 8 loose.
Don't add 8 and 10 for 8 trays. Count 8 tens.
Don't write the loose number first.

learn.hook: Snap 10 small blocks together. You get one long stick!
points: 10 single blocks join to make 1 block stick.
A stick or ten strip stands for 10. One small square is 1 unit.
Count sticks in tens, then count units in ones.
In 46, the left digit 4 tells the tens. The right digit 6 tells the ones.

example.q: There are 3 sticks and 6 units. What number is it?

learn.reallife: Bundles of 10 straws or sticks help us count big numbers in class.

quiz.q: How many single blocks make one block stick?
quiz.explain: A block stick is 10 blocks joined together.
steps: A block stick is blocks joined in a line.
quiz.mistake: Does not know a stick stands for ten

quiz.q: Pinky has 4 sticks and 2 units. What number is it?
quiz.explain: 4 sticks are 40. 2 units make 42.
quiz.mistake: Swaps tens and ones, or adds the digits

quiz.q: How many sticks and units make 63?
quiz.explain: 6 is the tens digit, so 6 sticks. 3 is the ones digit, so 3 units.
quiz.mistake: Reads the digits the wrong way round

quiz.q: In 29, what does the 2 tell us?
quiz.explain: The left digit is the tens digit. 2 tens means 20.
steps: In 29, 2 is on the left. Left digit = tens.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every digit means ones

quiz.q: Fill the table: 5 tens and 0 ones make ___.
quiz.explain: 5 tens is 50. With 0 ones, the number stays 50.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 0 in the ones place

quiz.q: Nikhil has 2 sticks and 15 units. What number is it?
quiz.explain: 15 units make 1 more stick and 5 units. So 3 sticks and 5 units = 35.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits side by side

teach.ask: Gappu: What is the difference between a stick and a unit?
teach.praise: Right! A stick is 10 blocks and a unit is just 1 block.
teach.nudge: How many blocks are in one stick? And in one unit?

revise.summary: 10 single blocks join to make 1 block stick. Count sticks in tens and units in ones; in 46, 4 tells the tens and 6 tells the ones.
focus: Read a number from sticks and units.
Show a number as sticks and units.
Know what each digit of a 2-digit number tells.
remember: 10 single blocks make 1 block stick.
A stick stands for 10. One small square is 1 unit.
The left digit tells the tens. The right digit tells the ones.
traps: Don't read the digits the wrong way round.
Don't forget the 0 in the ones place: 5 tens and 0 ones is 50.
15 units make 1 more stick and 5 units. Don't write the digits side by side.

learn.hook: Put ten sticks of ten together. You get a big number called one hundred!
points: 10 tens make 100. We say one hundred.
Count on in tens: 10, 20, 30 ... 90, 100.
Count on in ones near the end: 97, 98, 99, 100.
Strips of two colours can make 100: 6 red tens and 4 blue tens.

example.q: Ria has 7 red strips of ten. How many blue strips does she need to make 100?

learn.reallife: Ten ₹10 notes are the same as one ₹100 note.

games.title: Count on in tens
games.prompt: Count on in tens up to 100

quiz.q: How many tens make 100?
quiz.explain: Count in tens: 10, 20, 30 ... 100. That is 10 tens.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 100 tens make 100

quiz.q: Count on in tens: 60, 70, 80, ___
quiz.explain: Add 10 each time. 80 and 10 more is 90.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 10

quiz.q: Count on in ones: 96, 97, 98, ___
quiz.explain: Add 1 each time. After 98 comes 99.
quiz.mistake: Jumps by 10 instead of 1

quiz.q: Which number do we say after 99?
quiz.explain: 99 and 1 more is 100. Ten tens make 100.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the number after 99 is 910 or 110

quiz.q: Sonu joins 6 red strips and 4 blue strips of ten. How many squares in all?
quiz.explain: 6 tens and 4 tens make 10 tens. 10 tens is 100.
quiz.mistake: Counts strips, not squares

quiz.q: How many rupees do ten ₹10 notes make?
quiz.explain: Count in tens: 10, 20 ... 100. Ten ₹10 notes make ₹100.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 and 10 only once

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I make 100 using sticks of ten?
teach.praise: Yes! Ten sticks of ten make one hundred.
teach.nudge: How many sticks of ten do I need for 100?

revise.summary: 10 tens make 100, which we say as one hundred. We can count on in tens up to 100, or in ones: 97, 98, 99, 100.
focus: Count on in tens to 100.
Find how many more tens make 100.
Say the number after 99.
remember: 10 tens make 100.
99 and 1 more is 100.
Ten ₹10 notes are the same as one ₹100 note.
traps: Don't think 100 tens make 100. It is 10 tens.
The number after 99 is 100, not 910 or 110.
Count the squares, not just the strips.

topics.title: Writing numbers as tens and ones

learn.hook: Can you break 47 into two parts? A tens part and a ones part!
points: A tens card shows 10. A ones card shows 1.
4 tens and 7 ones make 47.
We can write 47 as 40 + 7. This is called expanding the number.
60 has 6 tens and 0 ones, so 60 = 60 + 0.

example.q: Write 85 in tens and ones, then expand it.

learn.reallife: To pay ₹47, give four ₹10 notes and seven ₹1 coins.

games.title: True or false?
items: The 7 is in the tens place, so it means 70. 72 = 70 + 2.
To show 34 we draw 4 tens cards and 3 ones cards

quiz.q: 4 tens and 7 ones make ___.
quiz.explain: 4 tens is 40. 40 and 7 ones is 47.
quiz.mistake: Adds the digits or writes them the wrong way

quiz.q: Which is the expanded form of 63?
quiz.explain: 6 is in the tens place, so it means 60. 3 is ones. 63 = 60 + 3.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the tens digit means tens

quiz.q: Asha draws tens and ones cards for 52. How many tens cards does she draw?
quiz.explain: 52 has 5 tens and 2 ones. So she draws 5 tens cards.
quiz.mistake: Picks the ones digit

quiz.q: Raju shows 38 with cards. How many ones cards does he draw?
quiz.explain: 38 is 3 tens and 8 ones. He draws 8 ones cards.
quiz.mistake: Picks the tens digit

quiz.q: 9 tens and 0 ones make ___.
quiz.explain: 9 tens is 90. 0 ones adds nothing.
quiz.mistake: Drops the 0 and writes 9

quiz.explain: 70 is 7 tens. Add 5 ones to get 75.
quiz.mistake: Writes all the digits side by side

teach.ask: Gappu: How can I break 47 into two parts?
teach.praise: Super! 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones, that is 40 + 7.
teach.nudge: What does the 4 in 47 stand for? And the 7?

revise.summary: A tens card shows 10 and a ones card shows 1. We can write 47 as 4 tens and 7 ones, or as 40 + 7; this is called expanding the number.
focus: Make a number from tens and ones.
Write the expanded form, like 63 = 60 + 3.
Count how many tens cards and ones cards a number needs.
remember: 4 tens and 7 ones make 47.
47 = 40 + 7 is the expanded form.
traps: Don't drop the 0: 9 tens and 0 ones is 90, not 9.
Don't mix up the tens digit and the ones digit.
Don't write all the digits side by side: 70 + 5 is 75.

learn.hook: Is 27 the same as 72? No way! Let us find out which one is more.
points: To compare two numbers, look at the tens first.
27 is less than 72 because 2 tens are less than 7 tens.
If the tens are the same, compare the ones: 45 is more than 43.
Swapping the digits makes a new number: 67 and 76 are different.

example.q: Which is more, 53 or 35?

learn.reallife: Bus 76 and bus 67 go to different places. Read the number carefully!

games.title: True or false?
items: 35 has 3 tens and 53 has 5 tens. So 35 is less.
The tens are the same. 6 ones are more than 2 ones.
67 is 6 tens 7 ones. 76 is 7 tens 6 ones.

quiz.q: Which is more: 27 or 72?
quiz.explain: 72 has 7 tens. 27 has only 2 tens. So 72 is more.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the ones digit

quiz.q: Tara has 38 beads. Bunty has 34 beads. Who has more?
quiz.explain: Both have 3 tens. Then compare ones: 8 is more than 4. Tara has more.
quiz.mistake: Stops when the tens are the same

quiz.q: Fill in: 45 is ___ than 54.
quiz.explain: 45 has 4 tens. 54 has 5 tens. So 45 is less.
steps: 4 tens < 5 tens, so 45 is less than 54.
quiz.mistake: Compares the ones digits first

quiz.q: Which number is more than 60?
quiz.explain: 61 is 1 more than 60. The others are less than 60.
steps: We need a number bigger than 60.
quiz.mistake: Is confused by the digit 6 in 16

quiz.q: Which number is less than 25?
quiz.explain: 19 has 1 ten. 25 has 2 tens. So 19 is less.
steps: We need a number smaller than 25.
1 ten < 2 tens, so 19 is less. Answer: 19
quiz.mistake: Thinks 52 is less because it uses the same digits

quiz.q: Swap the digits of 53 to get 35. Which is true?
quiz.explain: 35 has 3 tens and 53 has 5 tens. Swapping made a smaller number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks same digits make the same number

teach.ask: Gappu: Which is more, 27 or 72? How do you know?
teach.praise: Yes! Look at the tens first. 7 tens beat 2 tens!
teach.nudge: Which place should I look at first?

revise.summary: To compare two numbers, look at the tens first. If the tens are the same, compare the ones.
focus: Tell which number is more or less.
Compare the ones when the tens are the same.
See that swapping digits makes a new number.
remember: Compare the tens first. If the tens are the same, compare the ones.
27 is less than 72 because 2 tens are less than 7 tens.
traps: Don't look only at the ones digit.
Don't stop when the tens are the same; then compare the ones.
67 and 76 are not the same number.

learn.hook: Pick two digit cards. Put one in tens and one in ones. You made a number!
points: Digit cards 0 to 9 can go in the tens place or the ones place.
With cards 4 and 7 we can make 47 or 74.
For the larger number, put the bigger digit in tens.
For the smaller number, put the smaller digit in tens (never 0).

example.q: Make the largest and the smallest number with cards 3 and 8.
steps: Largest: bigger digit 8 in tens, so 83.
Smallest: smaller digit 3 in tens, so 38.

learn.reallife: Bus numbers, house numbers and lift buttons are all made from digits.

quiz.q: Using cards 5 and 2 once each, which is the largest number?
quiz.explain: Put the bigger digit 5 in tens: 52. 55 uses the 5 card twice.
quiz.mistake: Puts the smaller digit in tens

quiz.q: Using cards 6 and 4 once each, which is the smallest number?
quiz.explain: Put the smaller digit 4 in tens: 46. 44 uses the 4 card twice.
quiz.mistake: Puts the bigger digit in tens

quiz.q: With cards 3 and 7, make a number greater than 50.
quiz.explain: 73 has 7 tens, so it is more than 50. 37 has only 3 tens.
quiz.mistake: Does not check the tens digit

quiz.q: With cards 4 and 5, which number is between 40 and 50?
quiz.explain: 45 has 4 tens, so it is in the forties. 54 is more than 50.
steps: So 4 goes in the tens place: 45.
quiz.mistake: Picks the larger number

quiz.q: Gopi swaps the cards in 18 to get 81. Which is true?
quiz.explain: 81 has 8 tens. 18 has 1 ten. Swapping made a bigger number.
steps: 8 tens > 1 ten, so 81 is more than 18.
quiz.mistake: Thinks swapping does not change the value

quiz.q: Using cards 0 and 7 once each, which 2-digit number can we make?
quiz.explain: 0 cannot go in the tens place. So the only 2-digit number is 70.
steps: So 7 goes in tens, 0 in ones.
quiz.mistake: Puts 0 in the tens place

teach.ask: Gappu: I have cards 2 and 9. How do I make the biggest number?
teach.praise: Yes! Put the bigger digit in the tens place: 92!
teach.nudge: Which card should go in the tens place?

revise.summary: Digit cards can go in the tens place or the ones place. Put the bigger digit in tens for the larger number and the smaller digit in tens for the smaller number.
focus: Make the largest and smallest number from two cards.
Make a number that fits a clue, like between 40 and 50.
Know where 0 can go.
remember: For the larger number, put the bigger digit in tens.
For the smaller number, put the smaller digit in tens (never 0).
traps: Don't use one card twice: 55 is not allowed with cards 5 and 2.
Don't put 0 in the tens place.
Swapping the cards changes the value: 81 is more than 18.

learn.hook: Which is the smallest 2-digit number? Which is the biggest? Let us line them up!
points: The smallest 2-digit number is 10.
The largest 2-digit number is 99.
99 and 1 more is 100. 100 has three digits, so 99 is the largest 2-digit number.
Increasing order goes smallest to largest. Decreasing order goes largest to smallest.

example.q: Put 45, 12, 78, 30 in increasing order.

learn.reallife: Children stand in a line by height, or by roll number, from smallest to largest.

games.title: True or false?
items: 9 has one digit. 10 is the first number with two digits.
In increasing order, the biggest number comes first
Increasing order starts with the smallest.
10 is smaller than 11 and has 2 digits.

quiz.q: What is the smallest 2-digit number?
quiz.explain: 1 to 9 have one digit. 10 is the first number with two digits.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 11 or 1 is the smallest 2-digit number

quiz.q: What is the largest 2-digit number?
quiz.explain: 99 has the biggest digit, 9, in both places.
steps: Put the biggest digit, 9, in both places.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 100 is a 2-digit number

quiz.q: Why is 99 the largest 2-digit number?
quiz.explain: 99 + 1 = 100, and 100 has three digits. So no 2-digit number is bigger than 99.
steps: So no 2-digit number is bigger than 99.
Answer: The next number, 100, has 3 digits
quiz.mistake: Thinks counting stops at 99

quiz.q: Which list is in increasing order?
quiz.explain: Increasing means getting bigger: 14, then 29, then 53, then 80.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up increasing and decreasing

quiz.q: Which list is in decreasing order?
quiz.explain: Decreasing means getting smaller: 91, 67, 40, 18.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up decreasing and increasing

quiz.q: Put 36, 63 and 30 from largest to smallest. Which comes first?
quiz.explain: 63 has 6 tens, the most. So 63 comes first.
quiz.mistake: Starts with the smallest number

teach.ask: Gappu: What are the smallest and largest 2-digit numbers?
teach.praise: Correct! 10 is the smallest and 99 is the largest.
teach.nudge: Which is the first number with two digits? And the last?

revise.summary: The smallest 2-digit number is 10 and the largest is 99. Increasing order goes smallest to largest; decreasing order goes largest to smallest.
focus: Know the smallest and largest 2-digit numbers.
Explain why 99 is the largest 2-digit number.
Put numbers in increasing or decreasing order.
remember: Smallest 2-digit number: 10. Largest 2-digit number: 99.
99 and 1 more is 100, which has three digits.
Increasing: smallest to largest. Decreasing: largest to smallest.
traps: 100 is not a 2-digit number.
Don't mix up increasing and decreasing order.
The smallest 2-digit number is 10, not 11 or 1.

learn.hook: I have two digits. I am the largest with different digits. Who am I?
points: Read the clues one at a time.
The largest 2-digit number with different digits is 98.
The smallest 2-digit number with the same digits is 11.
The smallest number with 3 tens is 30. The largest is 39.
You can make your own riddles using tens and ones clues!

example.q: I have 6 tens. My ones digit is 2 more than my tens digit. Who am I?
steps: 6 tens: the number is in the sixties.

learn.reallife: Play number riddles with friends on a long train ride.

quiz.q: I am the largest 2-digit number with different digits. Who am I?
quiz.explain: 99 has the same digit twice. The next one down, 98, has different digits.
steps: One less is 98, with different digits. Answer: 98
quiz.mistake: Forgets the digits must be different

quiz.q: I am the smallest 2-digit number with both digits the same. Who am I?
quiz.explain: 10 has different digits. 11 is the first with the same digits.
steps: Start from the smallest: 10 has digits 1 and 0.
quiz.mistake: Gives the smallest 2-digit number instead

quiz.q: I am the smallest number with 3 tens. Who am I?
quiz.explain: 3 tens is 30. With 0 ones, 30 is the smallest.
quiz.mistake: Puts 3 in the ones place

quiz.q: I have 4 in the ones place. I am between 60 and 70. Who am I?
quiz.explain: Between 60 and 70 means 6 tens. With 4 ones, I am 64.
quiz.mistake: Puts 4 in the tens place

quiz.q: I have 2 tens. My ones digit is 5. Who am I?
quiz.explain: 2 tens is 20. Add 5 ones to get 25.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the tens and ones

quiz.q: Mini makes a riddle: 'I have 9 tens and 0 ones.' Who is she thinking of?
quiz.explain: 9 tens is 90, and 0 ones adds nothing.
quiz.mistake: Drops the 0

teach.ask: Gappu: Make me a riddle for the number 57!
teach.praise: Great riddle! 5 tens and 7 ones make 57.
teach.nudge: Can your riddle tell me the tens and the ones?

revise.summary: In a number riddle, read the clues one at a time and use tens and ones to find the number.
focus: Solve riddles with tens and ones clues.
Find the largest or smallest number that fits a rule.
Make your own riddles.
remember: Largest 2-digit number with different digits: 98.
Smallest 2-digit number with the same digits: 11.
Smallest number with 3 tens: 30. Largest: 39.
traps: Don't forget a clue, like 'digits must be different'.
Don't put the ones digit in the tens place.
Don't drop the 0: 9 tens and 0 ones is 90.

topics.title: First, second, third: the boat race

learn.hook: Splash! Five boats race to the finish line. Who came first?
points: Position words tell the order: first, second, third, fourth, fifth.
First is the one in front, the winner.
We can write them as 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th.
Second comes just after first. Fifth comes just after fourth.

example.q: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow and Pink boats finish in that order. Which position is Green?
steps: Green is next, so Green is 3rd.

learn.reallife: On Sports Day we say who came first, second and third in each race.

quiz.q: Boats finish: Rani, Dev, Isha, Om, Zoya. Who came first?
quiz.explain: Rani finished before everyone else, so she is first.
steps: Order: Rani, Dev, Isha, Om, Zoya.
quiz.mistake: Reads the order from the wrong end

quiz.q: Boats finish: Rani, Dev, Isha, Om, Zoya. In which position is Om?
quiz.explain: Rani 1st, Dev 2nd, Isha 3rd, Om 4th.
quiz.mistake: Counts one place too few or too many

quiz.q: Boats finish: Rani, Dev, Isha, Om, Zoya. Who came fifth?
quiz.explain: Zoya is the last of five, so she is fifth.
quiz.mistake: Counts from the end instead of the front

quiz.q: Which position comes just after second?
quiz.explain: First, second, then third.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of position words

quiz.q: Five boats race. Arif's boat is 3rd. How many boats are ahead of him?
quiz.explain: The 1st and 2nd boats are ahead of the 3rd boat. That is 2 boats.
quiz.mistake: Counts Arif's own boat too

quiz.q: Boats finish: Rani, Dev, Isha, Om, Zoya. Who is just after Dev?
quiz.explain: Dev is 2nd. Just after him is the 3rd boat, Isha.
quiz.mistake: Picks the boat just before Dev

teach.ask: Gappu: In a race, who is first and who is second?
teach.praise: Yes! First is in front and second comes just after.
teach.nudge: Who is right at the front? Who comes next?

revise.summary: Position words like first, second, third, fourth and fifth tell the order. First is the one in front, the winner.
focus: Find a position in a race from the front.
Write positions as 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th.
Tell who is just before or just after.
remember: First, second, third, fourth, fifth = 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th.
First is the one in front, the winner.
traps: Don't count from the end instead of the front.
Don't count your own boat when asked how many are ahead.
Just after means the next one, not the one before.

learn.hook: When is Onam this year? The calendar knows!
points: A calendar shows the days and dates of a month.
Each column is one day of the week, like Sunday or Monday.
Find the date, then look at the top of its column to get the day.
Dates in one column go up by 7: 1, 8, 15, 22, 29.

example.q: 1 August is a Friday. Which day is Independence Day, 15 August?

learn.reallife: Families look at the calendar to plan festivals, trips and holidays.

items.text: 1 August is a Friday, so 8 August is a ___
Dates in one column go up by ___
If the 3rd is a Monday, the 10th is a ___

games.title: True or false?
items: India celebrates Independence Day every year on 15 August.
If the 1st is a Friday, the 2nd is a Thursday
The day after Friday is Saturday.
Dates in one column of a calendar are 7 apart
Each row is one week of 7 days.

quiz.q: 1 September is a Monday. Onam is on 5 September. Which day is Onam?
quiz.explain: Count on: 1 Monday, 2 Tuesday, 3 Wednesday, 4 Thursday, 5 Friday.
quiz.mistake: Stops one day too early

quiz.q: On which date do we celebrate Independence Day?
quiz.explain: Independence Day is on 15 August. 26 January is Republic Day.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the national days

quiz.q: 1 August is a Friday. Raksha Bandhan is on the second Saturday. What is the date?
quiz.explain: The 1st is Friday, so the 2nd is the first Saturday. Add 7: the 9th is the second Saturday.
quiz.mistake: Takes the first Saturday

quiz.q: 1 August is a Friday. Which day is 15 August?
quiz.explain: 1, 8 and 15 are all in the same column, 7 apart. So 15 August is a Friday.
quiz.mistake: Counts on by one day too many

quiz.q: In a month, the 4th is a Sunday. What is the date of the next Sunday?
quiz.explain: A week has 7 days. 4 + 7 = 11.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 7

quiz.q: Diwali falls on Monday the 20th. Which day is the 21st?
quiz.explain: The day after Monday is Tuesday.
steps: The 21st is one day after the 20th.
The day after Monday is Tuesday.
quiz.mistake: Goes back a day instead of forward

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find the day of a festival on the calendar?
teach.praise: Yes! Find the date, then look up its column to see the day.
teach.nudge: Where do I look after I find the date?

revise.summary: A calendar shows the days and dates of a month. Find the date, then look at the top of its column to get the day.
focus: Find the day for a date.
Find the next same day by adding 7.
Find dates like the second Saturday.
remember: Each column is one day of the week.
Dates in one column go up by 7: 1, 8, 15, 22, 29.
Independence Day is on 15 August. Republic Day is on 26 January.
traps: Don't add 1 to find the next Sunday. Add 7.
Don't take the first Saturday when the second is asked.
Don't stop one day too early when counting on.

learn.hook: Dhum dhum! Did you know musical instruments have shapes too?
points: A dhol or drum is like a cylinder: two round flat ends and a curved side.
A ghatam is a round clay pot, shaped almost like a sphere.
A harmonium is box-like. Its shape is a cuboid.
A shehnai is thin at one end and wide at the other, a bit like a cone.
We hear these instruments at weddings, festivals and school functions.

example.q: How is the shape of a harmonium different from a dhol?
steps: Harmonium: flat faces and corners, like a box. It is a cuboid.
Dhol: two round flat ends and a curved side. It is a cylinder.
example.answer: Harmonium is a cuboid; dhol is a cylinder

learn.reallife: At a wedding baraat you may hear a dhol and a shehnai.

games.title: True or false?
items: A dhol is shaped like a cylinder
It has two round flat ends and a curved side.
A harmonium is round like a ball
A harmonium is box-like, a cuboid.
A ghatam is a round clay pot
It is played like a drum and is almost a sphere.
The dhol is often played at weddings and festivals
People dance to the dhol at baraats and festivals.
A shehnai is shaped like a cube
A shehnai is long, thin at one end and wide at the other.

quiz.q: A dhol has two round flat ends and a curved side. Which shape is it like?
quiz.explain: Round flat ends and a curved side make a cylinder.
steps: A dhol has two round flat ends.
Round flat ends + curved side = cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Thinks anything round is a sphere

quiz.q: A ghatam is a clay pot played as a drum. Its shape is most like a ___.
quiz.explain: A ghatam is round all over like a big ball, so it is sphere-like.
steps: A ghatam is round all over, like a big ball.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a pot with a box shape

quiz.q: A harmonium looks like a box. Which shape is it?
quiz.explain: A box shape with flat faces and corners is a cuboid.
steps: A harmonium looks like a box.
A box has flat faces and corners.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the name for a box shape

quiz.q: How is a harmonium different from a dhol?
options: Harmonium has corners; dhol has a curved side
quiz.explain: A harmonium is a cuboid with flat faces and corners. A dhol is a cylinder with a curved side.
steps: Harmonium is a cuboid: flat faces and corners.
Dhol is a cylinder: it has a curved side.
So the harmonium has corners; the dhol has a curved side.
Answer: Harmonium has corners; dhol has a curved side
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the faces of the two shapes

quiz.q: Which instrument is thin at one end and wide at the other, a bit like a cone?
quiz.explain: A shehnai gets wider towards its open end, like a cone.
steps: A cone is thin at the tip and wide at the base.
A shehnai gets wider towards its open end.
So the shehnai is like a cone.
quiz.mistake: Picks a box-shaped or round instrument

quiz.q: Which of these is shaped like a dhol?
quiz.explain: A gas cylinder has round flat ends and a curved side, just like a dhol.
steps: A gas cylinder has round flat ends and a curved side.
So a gas cylinder is shaped like a dhol.
quiz.mistake: Matches by size, not by shape

teach.ask: Gappu: What shape is a dhol? And a harmonium?
teach.praise: Yes! A dhol is a cylinder and a harmonium is a cuboid.
teach.nudge: Does the dhol have a curved side? Does the harmonium look like a box?

revise.summary: Musical instruments have solid shapes too. A dhol is like a cylinder, a ghatam is almost a sphere, a harmonium is a cuboid and a shehnai is a bit like a cone.
focus: Match each instrument to its solid shape.
Tell how a cuboid and a cylinder are different.
Match things by shape, not by size.
remember: Dhol: cylinder. Ghatam: almost a sphere.
Harmonium: cuboid. Shehnai: a bit like a cone.
traps: Don't think anything round is a sphere. A dhol has round flat ends and a curved side, so it is a cylinder.
Don't match by size. Match by shape.

learn.hook: A laddoo, a dice and a birthday cap. They all have shape names!
points: A sphere is round like a ball or a laddoo.
A cube is like a dice. All its faces are squares.
A cuboid is like a brick or a matchbox.
A cylinder is like a juice can or a drum.
A cone is like a birthday cap or an ice-cream cone.

example.q: Arjun sees a football, a brick and a juice can. Name their shapes.
steps: A football is round all over. It is a sphere.
A brick is like a box. It is a cuboid.
A juice can has round ends. It is a cylinder.

learn.reallife: Look in your kitchen. A gas cylinder, a sugar box and a round laddoo are all solid shapes.

games.title: Match the thing to its shape

quiz.q: A cricket ball looks like which shape?
quiz.explain: A ball is round all over, like a sphere.
steps: A cricket ball is round all over.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a sphere with a cylinder, which has flat ends

quiz.q: A dice is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: A dice has 6 faces and all of them are equal squares. That is a cube.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every box shape is a cuboid

quiz.q: Riya wears a party cap on her birthday. Its shape is a ___.
quiz.explain: A party cap has a round bottom and a pointed tip. That is a cone.
steps: A party cap has a round bottom.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a cone with a cylinder because both have a round face

quiz.q: A brick is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: A brick is a long box with flat faces. That is a cuboid.
steps: A brick is a long box.
It has flat faces, not all squares.
quiz.mistake: Calls a cuboid a cube even though its faces are not all equal squares

quiz.q: A can of juice is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: A can has a round top, a round bottom and a curved side. That is a cylinder.
steps: A can has a round top and round bottom.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a cylinder with a cone

quiz.q: Which one is NOT shaped like a sphere?
quiz.explain: A matchbox has flat faces and corners. It is a cuboid, not a sphere.
steps: Laddoo, football and marble are round all over: spheres.
A matchbox has flat faces and corners.
So the matchbox is not a sphere.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the word NOT

teach.ask: Gappu: What shape is a ball? And what shape is a dice?
teach.praise: Yes! A ball is a sphere and a dice is a cube. You know your shapes!
teach.nudge: What is the name of the round shape like a ball? And the dice shape?

revise.summary: Solid shapes are all around us. A ball is a sphere, a dice is a cube, a brick is a cuboid, a juice can is a cylinder and a birthday cap is a cone.
focus: Name the shape of everyday objects.
Tell a cube from a cuboid.
Tell a cylinder from a cone.
remember: Sphere: ball, laddoo. Cube: dice.
Cuboid: brick, matchbox. Cylinder: juice can, drum.
Cone: birthday cap, ice-cream cone.
traps: Don't call a cuboid a cube. All faces of a cube are equal squares.
Don't mix up a cylinder and a cone.
Read the word NOT carefully.

topics.title: Odd one out: flat and solid shapes

learn.hook: One of these is not like the others. Can you spot the odd one out?
points: Look at the shape of each object to find the odd one out.
Flat (2D) shapes like a circle or a square can be drawn on paper.
Solid (3D) shapes like a ball or a box can be held in your hand.
A circle is flat but a ball is solid. A square is flat but a dice is solid.

example.q: Find the odd one out: ball, orange, laddoo, brick.
steps: Ball, orange and laddoo are round like a sphere.

learn.reallife: A drawing of a ball is flat, but the real ball you kick is solid.

quiz.q: Find the odd one out: football, marble, dice, orange.
quiz.explain: Football, marble and orange are spheres. A dice is a cube.
steps: Football, marble, orange: round all over = spheres.
quiz.mistake: Looks at size or colour, not shape

quiz.q: Find the odd one out: juice can, drum, brick, candle.
quiz.explain: Can, drum and candle are cylinders. A brick is a cuboid.
steps: Can, drum, candle: round ends + curved side = cylinders.
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the shapes

quiz.q: Which of these is a flat shape?
quiz.explain: A circle can be drawn on paper. It is flat. The others are solids.
steps: A flat shape can be drawn on paper.
A circle is drawn on paper.
Can, ball and dice can be held: solids. Answer: Circle
quiz.mistake: Thinks a round solid like a ball is flat

quiz.q: Which of these is a solid shape?
quiz.explain: A matchbox can be held. It is a solid cuboid. The others are flat.
steps: A solid shape can be held in the hand.
A matchbox can be held: it is a cuboid.
Triangle, rectangle, square are flat. Answer: Matchbox
quiz.mistake: Mixes up flat and solid shapes

quiz.q: A square is flat. Which solid has faces that are squares?
quiz.explain: Every face of a cube is a square.
steps: Every face of a cube is a square.
quiz.mistake: Picks a solid with round faces

quiz.q: Find the odd one out: party cap, ice-cream cone, tennis ball, traffic cone.
quiz.explain: The cap and both cones are cone shapes. A tennis ball is a sphere.
steps: Party cap, ice-cream cone, traffic cone: all cones.
A tennis ball is round all over: a sphere.
quiz.mistake: Groups things by use, not by shape

teach.ask: Gappu: Is a circle the same as a ball?
teach.praise: Right! A circle is flat, and a ball is a solid you can hold.
teach.nudge: Can I hold a circle in my hand like a ball?

revise.summary: To find the odd one out, look at the shape of each object. Flat (2D) shapes can be drawn on paper; solid (3D) shapes can be held in your hand.
focus: Find the odd one out by shape.
Tell flat shapes from solid shapes.
Link a flat shape to a solid, like a square to a cube.
remember: Flat (2D): circle, square. Solid (3D): ball, box.
A circle is flat but a ball is solid.
traps: Don't group by size, colour or use. Group by shape.
A ball is solid, not flat.

learn.hook: Touch a dice. Flat parts, sharp lines and pointy tips! Each has a name.
points: A face is a flat side of a shape.
An edge is the line where two faces meet.
A corner is the pointy part where edges meet.
A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
A cuboid, like a matchbox, also has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
A sphere has no flat face, no edge and no corner.

example.q: How many faces does a dice have?

learn.reallife: Run your finger along a box. The sharp line you feel is an edge.

games.title: Match the shape to its faces
pairs: 1 round flat face and a tip

quiz.q: How many flat faces does a cube have?
quiz.explain: Top, bottom, front, back, left and right. That is 6 faces.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the faces that can be seen at one time

quiz.q: How many edges does a cube have?
quiz.explain: 4 edges on top, 4 on the bottom and 4 standing up. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up edges with faces or corners

quiz.q: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
quiz.explain: A cylinder has a flat circle on top and one at the bottom. Its side is curved.
steps: A cylinder has a flat circle on top.
It has one flat circle at the bottom. Its side is curved.
quiz.mistake: Counts the curved side as a flat face

quiz.q: Which shape has no flat face, no edge and no corner?
quiz.explain: A sphere is curved all over. It has nothing flat or pointy.
steps: A sphere is curved all over.
So it has no flat face, no edge, no corner.
quiz.mistake: Picks the cone, which has a flat face and a tip

quiz.q: A cone has how many flat faces?
quiz.explain: A cone has one flat circle at the bottom. The rest is curved up to the tip.
steps: A cone has one flat circle at the bottom.
The rest curves up to the tip.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a cone with a cylinder, which has 2 flat faces

quiz.q: Each face of a cube is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: All 6 faces of a cube are equal squares.
quiz.mistake: Does not look closely at the flat faces

teach.ask: Gappu: What is a face? What is an edge? I am confused!
teach.praise: Hooray! A face is flat, an edge is where faces meet, and a corner is pointy.
teach.nudge: Can you tell me about the corners too? Where do the edges meet?

revise.summary: A face is a flat side, an edge is where two faces meet, and a corner is where edges meet. A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
focus: Know the words face, edge and corner.
Count the faces, edges and corners of a cube.
Count the flat faces of a cylinder and a cone.
remember: Cube and cuboid: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 corners.
Cylinder: 2 flat faces. Cone: 1 flat face.
A sphere has no flat face, no edge and no corner.
traps: Don't count only the faces you can see.
A curved side is not a flat face.
Don't mix up edges with faces or corners.

topics.title: Decorate a box: faces, edges, corners

learn.hook: Let us decorate a box for Diwali! A star on every face, a ribbon on every edge, a pompom on every corner.
points: A cube has 6 faces, so it needs 6 stars.
A cube has 12 edges, so it needs 12 ribbon stripes.
A cube has 8 corners, so it needs 8 pompoms.
A cuboid, like a sweet box, also has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.

example.q: Ria puts one star on each face of a cube box. How many stars?

learn.reallife: Gift boxes and sweet boxes are cuboids with 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.

items.text: A cube needs ___ stars, one on each face
A cube needs ___ ribbons, one on each edge
A cube needs ___ pompoms, one on each corner

items.q: Stars for 2 cubes, one on each face

quiz.q: Anu sticks one star on every face of a cube box. How many stars does she need?
quiz.explain: A cube has 6 faces: top, bottom and 4 sides.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the faces she can see

quiz.q: Raj puts one ribbon stripe on every edge of a cube. How many stripes?
quiz.explain: A cube has 4 edges on top, 4 at the bottom and 4 standing up. That is 12.
quiz.mistake: Counts faces instead of edges

quiz.q: Meena puts one pompom on every corner of a cube. How many pompoms?
quiz.explain: A cube has 4 corners on top and 4 at the bottom. That is 8.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the top corners

quiz.q: A sweet box is a cuboid. How many faces does it have?
quiz.explain: A cuboid has 6 faces, just like a cube. Its faces are rectangles.
steps: A sweet box is a cuboid.
A cuboid has 6 faces, like a cube.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cuboid has fewer faces than a cube

quiz.q: How many corners does a matchbox have?
quiz.explain: A matchbox is a cuboid. It has 4 corners on top and 4 at the bottom.
steps: 4 corners on top, 4 at the bottom.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up corners and edges

quiz.q: Sam puts a star on every face of 2 cube boxes. How many stars?
quiz.explain: Each cube has 6 faces. 6 + 6 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Decorates only one box

teach.ask: Gappu: I want a star on every face and a pompom on every corner of a cube. How many of each?
teach.praise: Perfect! 6 stars for 6 faces and 8 pompoms for 8 corners.
teach.nudge: How many faces does a cube have? How many corners?

revise.summary: When we decorate a cube box, we need 6 stars for its faces, 12 ribbon stripes for its edges and 8 pompoms for its corners. A cuboid has the same numbers.
focus: Use faces, edges and corners to count decorations.
Know that a cuboid has the same count as a cube.
Count for two boxes.
remember: Cube: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 corners.
A cuboid also has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
traps: Don't count only the faces you can see.
Don't count faces when edges are asked.
Don't count only the top corners.

topics.title: Corners of cones, spheres and cylinders

learn.hook: Which solid has just one pointy corner? Let us count corners!
points: A cone has 1 corner (its tip) and 1 flat face (a circle).
A sphere has no corners, no edges and no flat face.
A cylinder has 2 flat faces and no corners.
A cube and a cuboid have many corners: 8 each.
We can fill a table: object, its shape, flat faces and corners.

example.q: Fill the table for a solid wooden cone: flat faces and corners.
steps: The round bottom is 1 flat face.

learn.reallife: A traffic cone on the road has one pointy tip: its only corner.

quiz.q: How many corners does a cone have?
quiz.explain: A cone has one pointed tip. That is its only corner.
steps: A cone has one pointed tip.
The tip is its only corner.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a curved shape has no corners at all

quiz.q: How many corners does a sphere have?
quiz.explain: A sphere is curved all over. It has no corners.
steps: A sphere is curved all over.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every solid has corners

quiz.q: How many corners does a cylinder have?
quiz.explain: A cylinder has 2 flat round faces and a curved side, but no corners.
steps: A cylinder has 2 flat round faces and a curved side.
quiz.mistake: Counts the flat faces as corners

quiz.q: Which object has no corners?
quiz.explain: A ball is a sphere, curved all over, so it has no corners.
steps: A ball is a sphere, curved all over.
So the ball has no corners.
quiz.mistake: Picks an object with flat faces

quiz.q: Which object has exactly one corner?
quiz.explain: A cone has one pointed tip, its only corner.
steps: An ice-cream cone has one tip.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a can has one corner

quiz.q: Name an object with 6 flat faces and 8 corners.
quiz.explain: A dice is a cube. A cube has 6 flat faces and 8 corners.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the faces and corners of a cube

teach.ask: Gappu: Which solids have no corners, and which have just one?
teach.praise: Great! A sphere and a cylinder have no corners. A cone has one tip.
teach.nudge: Which solid has a pointy tip? Which is curved all over?

revise.summary: A cone has 1 corner (its tip) and 1 flat face. A sphere and a cylinder have no corners, but a cube and a cuboid have 8 corners each.
focus: Count corners of a cone, sphere and cylinder.
Fill a table of object, shape, flat faces and corners.
Find an object from its faces and corners.
remember: Cone: 1 flat face, 1 corner.
Sphere: no corners. Cylinder: 2 flat faces, no corners.
Cube and cuboid: 8 corners each.
traps: Don't think every solid has corners.
Don't count flat faces as corners.
A cone does have one corner: its tip.

learn.hook: Push a ball and it rolls away. Push a brick and it just slides. Why?
points: A sphere is curved all over. It rolls.
A cube and a cuboid have flat faces. They slide and do not roll.
A cylinder can roll on its curved side and slide on its flat face.
Shapes with flat faces are easy to stack, one on top of another.

example.q: Kabir has a ball, a dice and a can. Which one can roll and also slide?
steps: The ball has no flat face. It rolls.
The dice has only flat faces. It slides.
The can has flat ends and a curved side. It can do both.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers stack boxes and cans on shelves, but keep oranges in a basket so they do not roll away.

games.title: True or false?
items: A ball is curved all over, so it rolls.
A brick rolls down a slope easily.
A brick has flat faces. It slides, it does not roll.
A cylinder can roll and also slide.
It rolls on its curved side and slides on its flat face.
We can stack cubes to make a tower.
Cubes have flat faces, so they sit well on each other.
A sphere has a flat face.
A sphere is curved all over. It has no flat face.

quiz.q: Which shape rolls but has no flat face to slide on?
quiz.explain: A sphere is curved all over. It has no flat face at all.
steps: A sphere is curved all over, so it has no flat face.
A cylinder rolls but also has flat faces. Answer: Sphere
quiz.mistake: Picks the cylinder, which does have two flat faces

quiz.q: Which shape can roll and also slide?
quiz.explain: A cylinder rolls on its curved side and slides on its flat face.
steps: Rolling needs a curved side. Sliding needs a flat face.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only one thing can happen for each shape

quiz.q: Meena wants to build a tall tower. Which shapes are best?
quiz.explain: Cubes have flat faces on top and bottom, so they stay on each other.
steps: A tower needs shapes that stay on each other.
Cubes have flat faces on top and bottom.
Balls roll off, cones have a tip. Answer: Cubes
quiz.mistake: Forgets that round shapes roll off

quiz.q: Why does a cube not roll?
quiz.explain: A cube has no curved side. All its faces are flat, so it slides.
steps: To roll, a shape needs a curved side.
A cube has only flat faces.
So it slides, it does not roll.
Answer: It has only flat faces
quiz.mistake: Thinks size or weight decides rolling

quiz.q: Kabir stands a can on its flat end and pushes it. What will it do?
quiz.explain: It is standing on its flat face, so it slides. It rolls only on its curved side.
steps: The can stands on its flat end.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cylinder always rolls

quiz.q: Which one will roll down a slope?
quiz.explain: A laddoo is round like a sphere, so it rolls. The others have flat faces.
steps: A round shape rolls down a slope.
A laddoo is round like a sphere.
Matchbox, brick, dice have flat faces. Answer: Laddoo
quiz.mistake: Does not notice which thing is round

teach.ask: Gappu: Why does my ball roll away but my toy brick just slides?
teach.praise: Now I see! Curved shapes roll and flat faces slide.
teach.nudge: What is different about the ball and the brick? Is it round or flat?

revise.summary: A sphere rolls, a cube and a cuboid slide, and a cylinder can roll on its curved side and slide on its flat face. Shapes with flat faces are easy to stack.
focus: Tell which shapes roll, slide or do both.
Choose shapes that stack well.
Explain why a cube does not roll.
remember: A sphere rolls. A cube and a cuboid slide.
A cylinder rolls on its curved side and slides on its flat face.
Shapes with flat faces are easy to stack.
traps: A cylinder does not always roll. On its flat end it slides.
Size or weight does not decide rolling. Shape does.

learn.hook: Can you make a solid with only 4 faces? Grab a cardboard sheet!
points: Draw a big triangle and split it into 4 small triangles.
Fold up the 3 outer triangles and tape them. You get a solid with 4 faces.
Every face of this solid is a triangle. It has 4 corners.
A ball has only one face. It is curved all over.

example.q: How many faces does the folded triangle solid have?
steps: 3 triangles fold up and meet at the top.

learn.reallife: Some paper toys and tea bags are shaped like this 4-face solid.

games.title: True or false?
items: A ball has only one face, and it is curved
A ball is curved all over, with no flat face.
We fold up 3 small triangles to make the 4-face solid
They fold up around the middle triangle.
A cone has only one face
A cone has a flat face and a curved face.

games.title: Make the solid
items: Draw a big triangle and mark 4 small triangles in it

quiz.q: How many faces does the solid made from 4 small triangles have?
quiz.explain: 1 triangle at the bottom and 3 folded up. 1 + 3 = 4 faces.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the bottom triangle

quiz.q: What shape is each face of the 4-face solid?
quiz.explain: It was made from 4 small triangles, so every face is a triangle.
steps: The solid is made of 4 small triangles.
So every face is a triangle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all solids have square faces

quiz.q: How many corners does the 4-face solid have?
quiz.explain: 3 corners at the bottom and 1 at the top where the triangles meet. 3 + 1 = 4.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the bottom corners

quiz.q: Which object has only one face, curved all over?
quiz.explain: A ball has one curved face and no flat faces.
steps: A ball has no flat face.
It has one curved face all over.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a drum has one face

quiz.q: How many small triangles fold up around the middle triangle?
quiz.explain: There are 4 small triangles. The middle one stays down, so 3 fold up.
quiz.mistake: Counts the middle triangle too

quiz.q: Which has more faces: a cube or the 4-face solid?
quiz.explain: A cube has 6 faces. 6 is more than 4.
steps: Cube: 6 faces. The new solid: 4 faces.
So the cube has more faces.
quiz.mistake: Does not remember a cube has 6 faces

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I make a solid with 4 faces from a cardboard sheet?
teach.praise: Wow! 4 triangles folded and taped make a 4-face solid.
teach.nudge: What shape should I cut? What do I do with the parts?

revise.summary: Fold the 3 outer triangles of a big split triangle to make a solid with 4 faces. Every face is a triangle and it has 4 corners.
focus: Count the faces and corners of the 4-face solid.
Know the shape of its faces.
Compare it with a cube.
remember: 4-face solid: 4 triangle faces, 4 corners.
A ball has only one face, curved all over.
traps: Don't forget the bottom triangle when counting faces.
Don't count only the bottom corners.
Not all solids have square faces.

learn.hook: A ginladi has 100 beads on 10 wires. Let us count them in tens!
points: A ginladi is a bead frame with 10 rows and 10 beads in each row.
10 rows of 10 beads make 100 beads.
To find 38, count 3 full rows and then 8 more beads.
A missing number is found by counting the beads before it.

example.q: Where does the card 65 go on the ginladi?
steps: Count 5 more beads in the next row: 61, 62, 63, 64, 65.

learn.reallife: Long ago, many shopkeepers added money on a bead frame.

items.text: After 4 full rows, the next bead is number ___
The 10th bead of row 3 is number ___

quiz.q: A ginladi has 10 rows with 10 beads each. How many beads in all?
quiz.explain: Count in tens 10 times: 10, 20 ... 100.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 and 10 instead of counting 10 rows

quiz.q: Tara counts 3 full rows and 8 more beads. Which card should she place there?
quiz.explain: 3 full rows are 30. 8 more beads make 38.
quiz.mistake: Swaps rows and beads

quiz.q: How many full rows of beads come before the bead numbered 44?
quiz.explain: 4 full rows hold beads 1 to 40. Bead 44 is in the next row.
quiz.mistake: Counts the row that bead 44 is in

quiz.q: A card is missing between 57 and 59 on the ginladi. What is it?
quiz.explain: The number between 57 and 59 is 58.
steps: The missing number is between 57 and 59.
quiz.mistake: Gives a number outside the gap

quiz.q: Which bead is the last bead of the 6th row?
quiz.explain: 6 full rows of 10 end at 60.
steps: Each row on the ginladi has 10 beads.
The last bead of the 6th row is 60.
quiz.mistake: Counts 6 beads instead of 6 rows

quiz.q: Ravi has counted 9 full rows. How many more beads to reach 100?
quiz.explain: 9 rows are 90 beads. One more row of 10 makes 100.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only 1 bead is left

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find bead number 38 on the ginladi?
teach.praise: Yes! 3 full rows, then 8 more beads.
teach.nudge: How many full rows should I count first?

revise.summary: A ginladi is a bead frame with 10 rows of 10 beads, so it has 100 beads. To find 38, count 3 full rows and then 8 more beads.
focus: Find a number on the ginladi using full rows and extra beads.
Find the last bead of a row.
Find how many more beads to reach 100.
remember: 10 rows of 10 beads make 100 beads.
38 = 3 full rows and 8 more beads.
traps: Don't add 10 and 10 for 10 rows. Count in tens 10 times.
Don't swap rows and beads.
Don't count the row that the bead is in as a full row.

learn.hook: From 1 to 100! Can you climb the number ladder to the top?
points: The number just after is 1 more. After 49 comes 50.
The number just before is 1 less. Before 70 comes 69.
The number between 37 and 39 is 38.
After 99 comes 100. We read it as one hundred.
Number names: 64 is sixty-four, 70 is seventy.

example.q: Which numbers come just before and just after 60?

learn.reallife: Seat numbers on a train go 1, 2, 3 and up. House numbers on a street are in order too.

quiz.q: Which number comes just after 49?
quiz.explain: Just after means 1 more. 49 + 1 = 50.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number just before, or adds 10

quiz.q: Which number comes just before 70?
quiz.explain: Just before means 1 less. 70 − 1 = 69.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number just after instead

quiz.q: Which number is between 37 and 39?
quiz.explain: 37, 38, 39. The number in the middle is 38.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number outside the two numbers

quiz.q: How do we write sixty-four in numbers?
quiz.explain: Sixty is 6 tens and four is 4 ones. So it is 64.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the tens and ones, or writes 60 and 4 side by side

quiz.q: What comes just after 99?
quiz.explain: 99 + 1 = 100. We read it as one hundred.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the count stops at 99

quiz.q: Joseph counts train coaches: 21, 22, 23, ___, 25. Which is missing?
quiz.explain: Counting on by 1: 23 + 1 = 24. Then 24 + 1 = 25.
quiz.mistake: Skips a number or swaps the digits

teach.ask: Gappu: What number comes just after 49? How do you know?
teach.praise: Yes! Just after means one more. 49 and one more is 50.
teach.nudge: How much more is the number just after?

revise.summary: The number just after is 1 more and the number just before is 1 less. After 99 comes 100, which we read as one hundred.
focus: Find the number just before, just after and between.
Write number names as numbers, like sixty-four = 64.
Fill a missing number in a counting list.
remember: Just after = 1 more. Just before = 1 less.
After 99 comes 100 (one hundred).
traps: Don't mix up just before and just after.
Don't write sixty-four as 604. It is 64.
The count does not stop at 99.

learn.hook: Tie 10 sticks into a bundle. Now counting is super quick!
points: 10 ones make 1 ten.
In 47, the 4 means 4 tens and the 7 means 7 ones.
The tens digit is on the left. The ones digit is on the right.

example.q: Aisha has 5 bundles of 10 sticks and 3 loose sticks. How many sticks?

learn.reallife: ₹10 notes are like tens and ₹1 coins are like ones when you count money.

quiz.q: How many tens are there in 58?
quiz.explain: In 58, the 5 is in the tens place. So there are 5 tens and 8 ones.
quiz.mistake: Picks the ones digit instead of the tens digit

quiz.q: Riya has 3 bundles of 10 sticks and 6 loose sticks. How many sticks?
quiz.explain: 3 tens is 30. 30 and 6 ones make 36.
quiz.mistake: Writes the ones first, or adds 3 and 6

quiz.q: What is the ones digit in 72?
quiz.explain: The ones digit is on the right. In 72 it is 2.
steps: The ones digit is on the right.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the tens digit and the ones digit

quiz.q: 4 tens and 0 ones make ___.
quiz.explain: 4 tens is 10, 20, 30, 40. With 0 ones, it is 40.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the 0 holds the ones place

quiz.q: Which is the same as 65?
quiz.explain: 65 has 6 in the tens place and 5 in the ones place.
steps: In 65, the left digit 6 is tens.
quiz.mistake: Reads the digits in the wrong places

quiz.q: Arjun has 2 notes of ₹10 and 7 coins of ₹1. How much money?
quiz.explain: 2 tens is ₹20. ₹20 and ₹7 make ₹27.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 and 7, or writes 20 and 7 side by side

teach.ask: Gappu: What does the 4 mean in 47?
teach.praise: Wow! 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones. That is 40 and 7!
teach.nudge: Is the 4 telling us tens or ones? And what about the 7?

revise.summary: 10 ones make 1 ten. In 47, the 4 means 4 tens and the 7 means 7 ones, so 47 = 40 + 7.
focus: Find the tens digit and the ones digit.
Make a number from bundles of 10 and loose sticks.
Count money with ₹10 notes and ₹1 coins.
remember: 10 ones make 1 ten.
Tens digit on the left. Ones digit on the right.
traps: Don't mix up the tens digit and the ones digit.
Don't add 3 and 6 for 3 tens and 6 ones. It is 36.
Don't forget the 0: 4 tens and 0 ones is 40.

learn.hook: Who has more laddoos? Let's find out with the hungry crocodile sign!
points: Look at the tens first. More tens means a bigger number.
If the tens are the same, look at the ones.
> means greater than. < means less than. = means equal.
The open mouth of > or < always faces the bigger number.

example.q: Compare 46 and 43.

learn.reallife: We compare scores in cricket and prices in the market to see which is more.

games.title: True or false?
items: Both have 4 tens, but 8 ones is more than 0 ones. So 48 > 40.
75 has 7 tens and 57 has 5 tens. They are not equal.
To compare 52 and 25, we look at the tens first.
The tens tell us more. 5 tens is more than 2 tens.

quiz.q: Which number is bigger: 45 or 54?
quiz.explain: 54 has 5 tens. 45 has only 4 tens. So 54 is bigger.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the ones digit first

quiz.q: Which sign goes in the gap? 67 ___ 76
quiz.explain: 67 has 6 tens and 76 has 7 tens. 67 is less, so 67 < 76.
steps: Compare tens: 67 has 6 tens, 76 has 7 tens.
quiz.mistake: Points the open mouth at the smaller number

quiz.q: Meena scored 38 runs. Kabir scored 35 runs. Who scored more?
quiz.explain: Both have 3 tens. 8 ones is more than 5 ones, so 38 > 35.
quiz.mistake: Stops after seeing the tens are the same

quiz.q: Which is the smallest: 29, 92, 20 or 90?
quiz.explain: 29 and 20 have the fewest tens. 0 ones is less than 9 ones, so 20 is smallest.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a number with 0 at the end is always big

quiz.q: Which sign goes in the gap? 50 ___ 50
quiz.explain: Both numbers are the same, so they are equal.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one side must always be bigger

quiz.q: Which number is greater than 81 but less than 85?
quiz.explain: 81, 82, 83, 84, 85. Only 83 is in the options and between them.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one of the two rules

teach.ask: Gappu: Is 45 bigger or 54 bigger? How do I check?
teach.praise: Brilliant! Look at the tens first. 54 has more tens, so it is bigger.
teach.nudge: Which digit should I look at first, the tens or the ones?

revise.summary: To compare numbers, look at the tens first; if the tens are the same, look at the ones. We use > for greater than, < for less than and = for equal.
focus: Compare two numbers using tens and ones.
Put the right sign >, < or = in the gap.
Find the smallest number or one between two numbers.
remember: > means greater than. < means less than. = means equal.
The open mouth of > or < faces the bigger number.
traps: Don't look at the ones digit first.
Don't point the open mouth at the smaller number.
Don't stop when the tens are the same. Compare the ones.

topics.title: Moving forward and back on a number strip

learn.hook: Hop, hop, hop! Moving forward on a number strip is like adding.
points: Start on a number and count each step you move.
Moving forward makes the number bigger. It is adding.
Moving back makes the number smaller. It is taking away.
From 12, 5 steps forward lands on 17. From 17, 3 steps back lands on 14.

example.q: Mani starts on 20. He moves 6 forward, then 2 back. Where does he stop?

learn.reallife: In Ludo and Snakes and Ladders you move forward on numbered boxes.

games.title: True or false?
items: Moving forward on a strip is like adding
Moving back makes the number bigger
To go from 40 to 46 you move 6 steps forward

quiz.q: Lata is on 12. She moves 5 steps forward. Where is she now?
quiz.mistake: Counts the starting box as a step

quiz.q: Kiran is on 30. He moves 4 steps back. Where is he now?
quiz.mistake: Moves forward instead of back

quiz.q: Ali is on 8. How many steps forward to reach 15?
quiz.explain: Count on from 8: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. That is 7 steps.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers

quiz.q: Moving back on a number strip is like ___.
quiz.explain: Each step back makes the number 1 less, so it is taking away.
steps: Each step back makes the number 1 less.
Making a number less is taking away.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up forward and back

quiz.q: Start on 20. Move 6 forward, then 3 back. Where do you stop?
quiz.explain: 20 forward 6 is 26. 26 back 3 is 23.
quiz.mistake: Does only one of the two moves

quiz.q: Pooja moves from 45 back to 40. How many steps did she move?
quiz.explain: Count back: 44, 43, 42, 41, 40. That is 5 steps.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the gap

teach.ask: Gappu: What happens to my number when I move forward or back?
teach.praise: Yes! Forward adds and makes it bigger. Back takes away and makes it smaller.
teach.nudge: Does moving back make my number bigger or smaller?

revise.summary: On a number strip, start on a number and count each step. Moving forward is adding and makes the number bigger; moving back is taking away and makes it smaller.
focus: Find where you land after moving forward or back.
Find how many steps between two numbers.
Do two moves one after the other.
remember: Forward = adding. Back = taking away.
From 12, 5 steps forward lands on 17.
traps: Don't count the starting box as a step.
Don't move forward when it says back.
Do both moves, not just one.

topics.title: Reading and marking a number line

learn.hook: A number line is a road for numbers. Every mark has a number!
points: Numbers on a number line go up by the same amount at each mark.
To read a mark, count on from the nearest number shown.
To mark 65 between 60 and 70, count 5 marks after 60.
You can draw a number line on the ground with chalk and jump on it!

example.q: A line shows 70 and 80, with small marks for each number between. Where is 79?

learn.reallife: A ruler is a number line. So is the dial on a weighing scale.

quiz.q: A number line goes 40, 41, 42, ?, 44. Which number is at the ? mark?
quiz.explain: Each mark is 1 more. After 42 comes 43.
steps: Each mark is 1 more than the one before.
quiz.mistake: Skips a mark

quiz.q: A number line shows 0, 10, 20, 30. Marks go up by 10. What comes after 30?
quiz.explain: Each mark adds 10. 30 + 10 = 40.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 10

quiz.q: To mark 65, you start at 60. How many small marks do you count on?
quiz.explain: 61, 62, 63, 64, 65. That is 5 marks after 60.
quiz.mistake: Counts the 60 mark too

quiz.q: Where is 79 on a line from 70 to 80?
quiz.explain: 79 is 1 less than 80, so it is the mark just before 80.
quiz.mistake: Reads the 7 in 79 as the ones

quiz.q: Sita draws a chalk line on the ground: 0, 2, 4, 6. What is the next mark?
quiz.explain: The marks go up by 2. 6 + 2 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 2

quiz.q: On a line from 20 to 30, a mark is 3 steps after 20. What number is it?
quiz.explain: Count on 3 from 20: 21, 22, 23.
quiz.mistake: Counts back instead of on

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find where 65 goes on a number line?
teach.praise: Super! Start at 60 and count 5 marks on.
teach.nudge: Which number should I start from? How many marks after it?

revise.summary: On a number line, numbers go up by the same amount at each mark. To read a mark, count on from the nearest number shown.
focus: Read a missing mark on a number line.
Find how much each mark goes up by.
Mark a number, like 65 between 60 and 70.
remember: To mark 65 between 60 and 70, count 5 marks after 60.
A ruler is a number line.
traps: Don't count the starting mark too.
Don't add 1 when the marks go up by 10 or 2.
Don't skip a mark.

learn.hook: A frog jumps 3 boxes each time: 1, 4, 7, 10 ... Can you guess the next?
points: Skip counting in 3s from 1: 1, 4, 7, 10, 13.
Skip counting in 5s from 40: 40, 45, 50, 55.
Skip counting in 10s from 50: 50, 60, 70, 80.
To find the rule, see how much is added each time. Add it again to extend the pattern.

example.q: Find the rule and the next number: 2, 5, 8, 11, ?

learn.reallife: Counting ₹5 coins: 5, 10, 15, 20. Counting ₹10 notes: 10, 20, 30.

quiz.q: Skip count in 3s: 1, 4, 7, 10, ___
quiz.explain: Each jump adds 3. 10 + 3 = 13.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 3

quiz.q: Skip count in 5s: 40, 45, 50, ___
quiz.explain: Each jump adds 5. 50 + 5 = 55.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 or 1 instead of 5

quiz.q: Skip count in 10s: 50, 60, 70, ___
quiz.explain: Each jump adds 10. 70 + 10 = 80.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 10

quiz.q: What is the rule? 6, 9, 12, 15
quiz.mistake: Guesses the rule from the first number

quiz.q: Find the next number: 12, 17, 22, 27, ___
quiz.explain: The rule is add 5. 27 + 5 = 32.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 to the last number

quiz.q: Ramu counts in 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Add 3 to 15 to get 18.
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 instead of 3

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find what comes next in 1, 4, 7, 10?
teach.praise: Yes! It adds 3 each time, so next is 13.
teach.nudge: How much is added each time?

revise.summary: Skip counting means adding the same number each time, like 3s, 5s or 10s. To find the rule, see how much is added each time, then add it again.
focus: Continue a skip-counting pattern.
Find the rule of a pattern.
Find the next number in a pattern.
traps: Don't add 1 when the rule is add 3 or add 5.
Don't guess the rule from the first number. Check each jump.

learn.hook: Colour the 2s red and the 5s blue on a 100 chart. Which numbers get both colours?
points: Counting in 2s on the chart: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 ...
Counting in 5s on the chart: 5, 10, 15, 20 ...
Numbers in both are 10, 20, 30 ... 100: the tens.
In 2s, 3s and 5s, the common numbers up to 100 are 30, 60 and 90.
In 5s and 7s, the common numbers up to 100 are 35 and 70.

example.q: Which numbers come in both counting in 5s and counting in 7s, up to 100?
steps: 5s end in 5 or 0. From the 7s, only 35 and 70 do.

learn.reallife: One bus comes every 2 minutes and another every 5 minutes. They arrive together every 10 minutes!

games.title: True or false?
items: 30 comes when counting in 2s, in 3s and in 5s
2s go 28, 30. 3s go 27, 30. 5s go 25, 30. All three reach 30.
35 comes when counting in 5s and in 7s
Counting in 2s gives even numbers. 15 is odd.
All tens like 10, 20, 30 come in both 2s and 5s
Tens end in 0, so both counts reach them.

quiz.q: Which number comes in both counting by 2s and counting by 5s?
quiz.explain: 40 is even, so 2s reach it. It ends in 0, so 5s reach it too.
steps: 2s give even numbers. 5s give numbers ending in 5 or 0.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number from only one list

quiz.q: Which number does NOT come when counting by 2s?
quiz.explain: Counting in 2s gives even numbers. 15 is odd.
steps: Counting by 2s gives even numbers only.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every number in the 5s also comes in the 2s

quiz.q: Up to 100, which numbers come in counting by 2s, 3s and 5s?
quiz.explain: They must be tens (for 2s and 5s) and also in the 3s: 30, 60 and 90.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to check the 3s

quiz.q: Which number comes in both counting by 5s and counting by 7s?
quiz.explain: 7s: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35. 35 ends in 5, so it is in the 5s too.
steps: 35 ends in 5, so 5s reach it too.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one of the two counts

quiz.q: Counting by 5s and by 7s up to 100, which two numbers are common?
quiz.explain: From the 7s, only 35 and 70 end in 5 or 0.
quiz.mistake: Does not check every number in the 7s

quiz.q: Counting by 2s and by 5s, what is the first number in both?
quiz.explain: 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. 5s: 5, 10. The first common number is 10.
quiz.mistake: Picks a starting number of one list

teach.ask: Gappu: Which numbers come when counting in 2s and also in 5s?
teach.praise: Yes! The tens like 10, 20, 30 are in both.
teach.nudge: Which numbers did both colours reach?

revise.summary: On the 100 chart some numbers come in two counts. In 2s and 5s, the common numbers are the tens: 10, 20, 30 ... 100.
focus: Find numbers that come in both 2s and 5s.
Find common numbers in 2s, 3s and 5s, or 5s and 7s.
Know that counting in 2s gives even numbers.
remember: 2s and 5s: common numbers are 10, 20, 30 ... 100.
5s and 7s up to 100: 35 and 70.
traps: Don't pick a number from only one list. Check both.
Don't forget to check the 3s too.
Not every number in the 5s comes in the 2s.

topics.title: Will the jumps land on it?

learn.hook: Counting in 10s from 10, will you land on 100? Let us check before we jump!
points: Counting in 10s from 10 goes 20, 30 ... 100. Yes, it lands on 100!
Counting in 2s from 4 gives only even numbers. It never lands on 17.
Counting in 5s from 5 lands only on numbers ending in 5 or 0.
Counting on from a number never gives numbers before it. From 20 you never say 15.

example.q: Start at 1 and count in 3s. Will you land on 10?

learn.reallife: Climb stairs two at a time from the ground: you land on steps 2, 4, 6 ...

games.title: True or false?
items: Counting on in 5s from 30, we will say 25
Counting on goes up: 35, 40. 25 is before 30.

quiz.q: Sonu counts in 2s starting from 4. Will he say 17?
options: No, he only says even numbers
quiz.explain: 4, 6, 8 ... 16, 18. Every number is even, so 17 never comes.
steps: 17 is odd, so he never says it.
Answer: No, he only says even numbers
quiz.mistake: Thinks counting in 2s says every number

quiz.q: Counting in 10s from 10, which of these will you say?
quiz.explain: 10s from 10 give numbers ending in 0. 100 comes.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number that does not end in 0

quiz.q: Counting in 5s from 5, which number will you land on?
quiz.explain: 5s land on numbers ending in 5 or 0. 65 ends in 5.
quiz.mistake: Does not look at the ones digit

quiz.q: Mira counts on in 2s from 20: 22, 24, 26 ... Will she say 18?
quiz.explain: Counting on only goes up from 20. 18 is less than 20.
steps: Counting on from 20 only goes up: 22, 24, 26 …
quiz.mistake: Thinks counting on can go backward

quiz.q: Counting in 3s from 1 (1, 4, 7 ...), which number will you land on?
quiz.mistake: Thinks counting in 3s lands on 9 and 12

quiz.q: Counting in 2s from 2, which number will you never say?
quiz.explain: Counting in 2s from 2 gives even numbers. 35 is odd.
steps: 35 is odd, so it never comes.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which numbers are even

teach.ask: Gappu: I count in 2s from 4. Will I ever say 17?
teach.praise: Right! Counting in 2s from 4 gives only even numbers, and 17 is odd.
teach.nudge: Are the numbers I say even or odd? What about 17?

revise.summary: Some jumps land on a number and some never do. Counting in 2s from 4 gives only even numbers, and counting on never gives numbers before the start.
focus: Tell if a count will land on a number.
Use the ones digit for counting in 5s and 10s.
Know that counting on only goes up.
remember: Counting in 5s from 5 lands only on numbers ending in 5 or 0.
Counting on from 20, you never say 15.
traps: Counting in 2s does not say every number.
Counting on cannot go backward.
Counting in 3s from 1 does not land on 9 or 12.

learn.hook: 10, 9, 8 ... 3, 2, 1, blast off! Let us count backward.
points: Counting backward goes down: 10, 9, 8, 7 ... 1.
From 20 to 0 takes 20 steps in ones but only 10 steps in twos.
If a list has no pattern, change a number to make one, then extend it.

example.q: Count back in 20s from 100. What are the next three numbers?
