learn.reallife: Before a race starts, we count backward: 3, 2, 1, go!

quiz.q: Count backward: 10, 9, 8, 7, ___
quiz.explain: Each number is 1 less. 7 - 1 = 6.
steps: Counting back: each number is 1 less.
quiz.mistake: Counts forward instead of back

quiz.q: Count back in 3s: 21, 18, 15, ___
quiz.explain: Take away 3 each time. 15 - 3 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 1 instead of 3

quiz.q: Count back in 20s: 100, 80, 60, ___
quiz.explain: Take away 20 each time. 60 - 20 = 40.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 10 instead of 20

quiz.q: Pinky counts back from 20 to 0 in twos. How many steps does she take?
quiz.mistake: Counts steps in ones instead of twos

quiz.q: Which list shows counting back in 5s?
quiz.explain: 60, 55, 50, 45 takes away 5 every time.
steps: Back in 5s: take away 5 each time.
quiz.mistake: Does not check every step

quiz.q: Fix the pattern of counting back in 10s: 40, 30, 25, 10. What should replace 25?
quiz.explain: Counting back in 10s from 30 gives 20. So 40, 30, 20, 10.
steps: Back in 10s: take away 10 each time.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 5 instead of 10

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I count back in 5s from 50?
teach.praise: Yes! 50, 45, 40 ... take away 5 each time.
teach.nudge: Should my numbers go up or down? By how much?

revise.summary: Counting backward goes down: 10, 9, 8, 7. We can also skip back in 3s, 5s, 10s or 20s by taking away the same number each time.
focus: Continue a backward count.
Count the steps when going back in twos.
Fix a wrong number in a backward pattern.
remember: From 20 to 0: 20 steps in ones, 10 steps in twos.
traps: Don't count forward when it says backward.
Don't take away 10 when the rule is take away 20.
Check every step of the pattern.

learn.hook: Colour 9, 19, 29 ... on a 100 chart. What do you see? A straight column!
points: Numbers ending in 9 make one straight column going down the chart.
Going down a column, each number is 10 more: 9, 19, 29.
The slanting line 1, 12, 23, 34 ... 100 goes up by 11 each time.
To describe a pattern, say what changes and by how much.

example.q: Continue the slanting pattern: 1, 12, 23, 34, ?

learn.reallife: Floor tiles often make column and slanting patterns.

items.text: Numbers ending in 9 make a ___ on the chart

games.title: True or false?
items: 9, 19, 29, 39 are each just before a ten
9 is before 10, 19 is before 20, and so on.
The slanting line 1, 12, 23 adds 10 each time
Going down a column, each number is 10 more

quiz.q: Which number comes just before 30?
quiz.explain: 1 less than 30 is 29.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number after instead of before

quiz.q: 9, 19, 29, 39, ___. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Each number is 10 more. 39 + 10 = 49.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 10

quiz.q: On the 100 chart, where are 9, 19, 29, 39 ... 99?
quiz.explain: They all end in 9, so they sit one under another in the same column.
steps: On the 100 chart, numbers ending in 9 are one under another.
So they are in one column, going down.
Answer: In one column, going down
quiz.mistake: Thinks the numbers are in a row

quiz.q: The slanting pattern goes 1, 12, 23, 34. How much is added each time?
quiz.mistake: Thinks it adds 10 like a column

quiz.q: Continue the slanting pattern: 56, 67, 78, ___
quiz.explain: Add 11 each time. 78 + 11 = 89.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 or 10 instead of 11

quiz.q: Rohan colours 5, 15, 25, 35 on the chart. How can we describe this pattern?
options: Each is 10 more than the one before
quiz.explain: 15 - 5 = 10, 25 - 15 = 10. Each number is 10 more.
steps: Each number is 10 more than the one before.
Answer: Each is 10 more than the one before
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the ones digit 5

teach.ask: Gappu: I coloured 9, 19, 29, 39 on the chart. What pattern did I make?
teach.praise: Yes! A straight column. Each number is 10 more and ends in 9.
teach.nudge: Where are these numbers on the chart? What do they end in?

revise.summary: The 100 chart has patterns. Going down a column, each number is 10 more, and the slanting line 1, 12, 23, 34 goes up by 11 each time.
focus: Continue a column pattern like 9, 19, 29.
Continue a slanting pattern that adds 11.
Describe a pattern: what changes and by how much.
remember: Down a column: 10 more each time.
Slanting line 1, 12, 23, 34 ... adds 11 each time.
traps: Numbers ending in 9 are in a column, not a row.
Don't add 10 for the slanting pattern. It adds 11.
Don't look only at the ones digit.

learn.hook: On a 100 chart, every number has neighbours: up, down, left and right!
points: The number to the right is 1 more. The number to the left is 1 less.
The number just below is 10 more. The number just above is 10 less.
For 45: left 44, right 46, above 35, below 55.
Use these rules to fill a window cut out from the chart.

example.q: Find the neighbours of 67.

learn.reallife: On a calendar, the date just below is 7 more. On a 100 chart, it is 10 more!

quiz.q: On a 100 chart, which number is just below 34?
quiz.explain: Just below means 10 more. 34 + 10 = 44.
steps: Just below on the chart means 10 more.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 10

quiz.q: On a 100 chart, which number is just above 58?
quiz.explain: Just above means 10 less. 58 - 10 = 48.
steps: Just above on the chart means 10 less.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 instead of taking away

quiz.q: On a 100 chart, which number is just to the right of 79?
quiz.explain: Right means 1 more. 79 + 1 = 80.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 instead of 1

quiz.q: On a 100 chart, which number is just to the left of 63?
quiz.explain: Left means 1 less. 63 - 1 = 62.
quiz.mistake: Moves right instead of left

quiz.q: A window from the chart has 26 in the middle. What is just below 26?
quiz.explain: Below is 10 more. 26 + 10 = 36.
quiz.mistake: Moves right instead of down

quiz.q: A chart window shows 14, 15 on top and 24, ___ below. What is missing?
quiz.explain: The missing box is below 15, so it is 15 + 10 = 25. It is also right of 24.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 to 15 instead of 10

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find the numbers around 45 on the chart?
teach.praise: Great! Left and right change by 1. Up and down change by 10.
teach.nudge: How much changes when I go down one box? And one box right?

revise.summary: On the 100 chart, the number to the right is 1 more and to the left is 1 less. The number just below is 10 more and just above is 10 less.
focus: Find all four neighbours of a number.
Fill a window cut out from the chart.
Know which way is 1 and which way is 10.
remember: Right: 1 more. Left: 1 less.
Below: 10 more. Above: 10 less.
For 45: left 44, right 46, above 35, below 55.
traps: Don't add 1 for the number below. Add 10.
Above is 10 less, not 10 more.
Don't move right when the question says down.

learn.hook: 1 block, then 3 blocks, then 5 ... The pattern keeps growing!
points: In a growing pattern, each shape is bigger than the one before.
See how many blocks are added each time.
Add the same amount again to find the next shape.
Square patterns: 1 block, then 2 rows of 2 (4 blocks), then 3 rows of 3 (9 blocks).

example.q: A pattern has 2, 4, 6 blocks. How many in the next shape?

learn.reallife: Steps of a staircase grow one block taller each time.

quiz.q: A pattern grows: 1, 3, 5 blocks. How many blocks in the next shape?
quiz.explain: Each step adds 2 blocks. 5 + 2 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 2

quiz.q: A staircase pattern has 1, 2, 3, 4 blocks. How many blocks are added each time?
quiz.explain: Each step is 1 block taller: 2 - 1 = 1.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total instead of the step

quiz.q: A square pattern has 1, then 4, then 9 blocks. How many blocks make 3 rows of 3?
quiz.explain: 3 rows of 3 is 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 3 only

quiz.q: Square pattern: 1, 4, 9. The next square has 4 rows of 4. How many blocks?
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 to 9 instead of making a square

quiz.q: Sapna adds 3 blocks each time: 3, 6, 9. How many in the next shape?
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 3

quiz.q: A tower pattern has 2, 4, 6, 8 blocks. How many blocks in the 5th tower?
quiz.explain: Each tower has 2 more. The 4th has 8, so the 5th has 10.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the last number

teach.ask: Gappu: My block pattern goes 1, 3, 5. How do I make the next shape?
teach.praise: Yes! Add 2 more blocks each time. Next is 7.
teach.nudge: How many blocks were added from one shape to the next?

revise.summary: In a growing pattern, each shape is bigger than the one before. See how many blocks are added each time and add the same amount again.
focus: Find how many blocks are added each time.
Find the next shape in a growing pattern.
Count blocks in square patterns.
remember: Square pattern: 1, then 2 rows of 2 (4), then 3 rows of 3 (9).
Add the same amount again to find the next shape.
traps: Don't add 1 when the pattern adds 2 or 3.
Don't give the total when asked how many are added.
A square pattern makes rows: 4 rows of 4 is 16, not 9 + 4.

learn.hook: Wave your hand in the sun. A dark hand waves back on the ground! That is your shadow.
points: A shadow forms when something blocks light.
People, trees and animals all make shadows in sunlight.
No light means no shadow. In a dark room, shadows vanish.
Bring a torch closer to a toy and its shadow grows bigger.
Our shadow is long in the early morning and evening, and shortest at noon.

example.q: Ravi stands in the sun at 7 in the morning and again at 12 noon. When is his shadow longer?
steps: In the early morning the sun is low in the sky.
A low sun makes a long shadow. At noon the sun is high, so the shadow is short.

learn.reallife: On a hot afternoon, cows rest in the shade of a big tree.

games.title: True or false?
items: A shadow forms when light is blocked
The object stops the light, so a dark shape forms behind it.
We can see our shadow in a fully dark room
Without light there is no shadow.
Our shadow is shortest at noon
At noon the sun is high above us.
Moving a torch closer to a toy makes its shadow smaller
A closer torch makes a bigger shadow.
A tree makes a shadow on a sunny day

quiz.q: When does a shadow form?
quiz.explain: An object stops the light. The dark patch behind it is the shadow.
steps: A shadow is a dark patch behind an object.
It forms when the object blocks light.
quiz.mistake: Thinks shadows come from darkness, not from light

quiz.q: Mona switches off every light in her room at night. What happens to her shadow?
quiz.explain: A shadow needs light. With no light, there is no shadow.
steps: With all lights off, there is no light.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a shadow is always there

quiz.q: Abu moves a torch closer to his toy elephant. What happens to its shadow on the wall?
quiz.explain: When the torch comes closer, the toy blocks more light, so the shadow grows.
steps: The toy blocks more of the light.
quiz.mistake: Thinks closer light makes a smaller shadow

quiz.q: At what time of day is your shadow the shortest?
quiz.explain: At noon the sun is high overhead, so the shadow is short.
steps: At noon the sun is high overhead.
High sun makes a short shadow.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up morning and noon shadows

quiz.q: Which of these makes a shadow in the sun?
quiz.explain: A tree is a thing that blocks sunlight, so it makes a shadow.
steps: A shadow needs a thing that blocks light.
Sound and smell cannot block light. Answer: A tree
quiz.mistake: Does not know only objects can block light

quiz.q: Rani sees that her shadow is very long. What time is it most likely?
quiz.explain: Shadows are long when the sun is low, in the early morning or evening.
steps: Long shadows come when the sun is low.
The sun is low in the early morning or evening.
At noon shadows are short. Answer: Early morning
quiz.mistake: Thinks the shadow is longest at noon

teach.ask: Gappu: Why do I see my shadow on a sunny day?
teach.praise: Yes! You block the sunlight, so a shadow forms.
teach.nudge: What does my body do to the sunlight?

revise.summary: A shadow forms when something blocks light, so no light means no shadow. Our shadow is long in the early morning and evening and shortest at noon.
focus: Explain how a shadow forms.
Tell when a shadow is long or short in the day.
Say what happens when a torch comes closer.
remember: A shadow forms when something blocks light.
No light means no shadow.
Shadow: long in early morning and evening, shortest at noon.
traps: Shadows come from light being blocked, not from darkness.
The shadow is not longest at noon. It is shortest then.
A closer torch makes the shadow bigger, not smaller.

topics.title: Flat shapes from shadows and tracing

learn.hook: Put a can on paper and draw around it. Surprise! A flat shape appears.
points: A shadow is flat. It shows a flat shape.
Draw around the face of a solid shape to get a flat shape.
The bottom of a can or a glass gives a circle.
A face of a dice gives a square. The long face of a brick gives a rectangle.
A party cap seen from the side makes a triangle shadow.

example.q: Harpreet puts a matchbox on paper on its big face and draws around it. What shape does she get?
steps: The big face of a matchbox is long and flat.
It has 4 straight sides and 4 corners.
Two sides are long and two are short.

learn.reallife: At night, make hand shadows on the wall with a torch. Shadows are flat pictures.

games.title: What shape will you get?
pairs: Side shadow of a party cap

games.title: True or false?
items: A shadow lies flat on the wall or the floor.
Drawing around a face of a dice gives a square.
Every face of a dice is a square.
A ball has a flat face we can draw around.
A ball is curved all over. It has no flat face.
Drawing around the bottom of a glass gives a triangle.
The bottom of a glass is round, so we get a circle.

quiz.q: Riya draws around the bottom of a juice can. What shape does she get?
quiz.explain: The bottom of a can is round. Drawing around it gives a circle.
steps: The bottom of a can is round.
Drawing around a round face gives a circle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of the side of the can, not its bottom

quiz.q: Arjun draws around one face of a dice. What shape does he get?
quiz.explain: Every face of a dice has 4 equal sides. That is a square.
steps: A dice face has 4 equal sides.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the solid cube with its flat face

quiz.q: Meena draws around the long face of a brick. What shape does she get?
quiz.explain: The long face has 2 long sides and 2 short sides. That is a rectangle.
steps: The long face of a brick has 2 long and 2 short sides.
quiz.mistake: Calls every 4-sided shape a square

quiz.q: Kabir shines a torch on a ball. What shape is its shadow on the wall?

quiz.q: Which solid shape can make a triangle shadow from the side?

steps: A party cap is a cone.
From the side: pointed top, flat bottom.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a dice can make a triangle

quiz.q: Which thing has a face you can draw around to get a square?
quiz.explain: A dice is a cube. Each of its faces is a square.
steps: A square face needs 4 equal sides.
A dice is a cube: each face is a square.
quiz.mistake: Picks a round object that gives a circle

teach.ask: Gappu: I drew around the bottom of a can. Why did I get a circle?
teach.praise: Yes! The flat bottom of a can is round, so it makes a circle.
teach.nudge: What shape is the flat bottom of the can?

revise.summary: A shadow is flat and shows a flat shape. Drawing around the face of a solid also gives a flat shape, like a circle, square, rectangle or triangle.
focus: Name the flat shape you get by drawing around a face.
Name the shadow shape of a solid.
Tell a square face from a rectangle face.
remember: Bottom of a can or glass: circle.
Face of a dice: square. Long face of a brick: rectangle.
A party cap seen from the side: triangle shadow.
traps: Don't call every 4-sided shape a square.
Draw around the bottom of the can, not its side.
A dice does not make a triangle. A party cap does.

learn.hook: A bangle, a roti and a samosa! Which ones are circles?

A triangle has 3 straight sides.
A triangle has 3 corners.

learn.reallife: A roti and a wheel are round like circles. A slice of pizza looks like a triangle.

quiz.mistake: Mixes up a triangle with a square

quiz.q: How many corners does a circle have?

quiz.q: Which of these looks like a circle?

steps: A shape with 3 straight sides is a triangle.

revise.summary: A circle is round with no straight sides and no corners. A triangle has 3 straight sides and 3 corners.

Know that a circle has no corners.
Find circles and triangles around us.
remember: Circle: no straight sides, no corners.
Triangle: 3 straight sides, 3 corners.
traps: A circle has 0 corners. The start of the drawing is not a corner.
Not every shape with straight sides is a square.
For 2 triangles, count the corners of both.

learn.hook: A carrom board and a classroom door both have 4 sides. But they look different!

A square has 4 corners.
A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 corners too.
In a rectangle, sides facing each other are the same. A door has 2 long and 2 short sides.

example.q: Kabir counts the corners on 1 square and 1 triangle. How many corners in all?

learn.reallife: A carrom board is a square. A door, a blackboard and a train ticket are rectangles.

quiz.q: How many sides does a square have?

quiz.mistake: Mixes up a square with a triangle

quiz.q: What is special about the 4 sides of a square?
options: They are all the same length
quiz.explain: All 4 sides of a square are equal. That is what makes it a square.
steps: All 4 sides are the same length.
That is what makes it a square.
Answer: They are all the same length
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a square with a rectangle like a door

quiz.q: A classroom door looks like a ___.
quiz.explain: A door has 4 sides: 2 long and 2 short. That is a rectangle.

quiz.q: How many corners do 1 square and 1 triangle have in all?

teach.nudge: Are all the sides the same length in both? Which one has long and short sides?

Count corners of squares, rectangles and triangles together.
Find squares and rectangles around us.

topics.title: Adding with blocks and in columns

points: A tens rod has 10 blocks. A small cube is 1.

teach.praise: Yes! Numbers in the table of 10 end in 0.
teach.nudge: What is the ones digit of 10, 20, 30?

revise.summary: The table of 5 goes 5, 10, 15 ... 50 and its answers end in 5 or 0. The table of 10 goes 10, 20, 30 ... 100 and its answers end in 0.
focus: Say the tables of 5 and 10.
Count fingers on hands and money in ₹10 notes.
Spot a number that is not in the table of 5.
remember: Table of 5 ends in 5 or 0. Table of 10 ends in 0.
traps: Don't write 6 and 10 side by side for 6 × 10. It is 60.
Don't add 8 and 5 for 8 × 5.
Check the ones digit: 32 is not in the table of 5.

topics.title: Turn it around: order in multiplication

learn.hook: 4 groups of 3, or 3 groups of 4. Which is more? Surprise: they are the same!
points: 3 groups of 4 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
So 4 × 3 = 3 × 4. Changing the order does not change the answer.
A picture of 4 rows of 5 shows 4 × 5 = 20 and 5 × 4 = 20.

example.q: Show that 6 × 4 = 4 × 6.

learn.reallife: 12 chairs can stand in 4 rows of 3 or 3 rows of 4. Still 12 chairs!

games.title: True or false?
items: Changing the order in multiplication changes the answer
4 rows of 5 is the same as 5 rows of 4

quiz.q: 4 groups of 3 make 12. How many do 3 groups of 4 make?
quiz.explain: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Turning the order around gives the same total.
steps: Turning the order around gives the same total.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a different order gives a different total

quiz.q: Which is the same as 5 × 4?
quiz.explain: Changing the order does not change the product: 5 × 4 = 4 × 5 = 20.
steps: Changing the order does not change the product.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up times and plus

quiz.q: A picture shows 4 rows of 6 flowers. How many flowers?
quiz.mistake: Adds the rows and the flowers in a row

quiz.q: If 6 × 4 = 24, what is 4 × 6?
quiz.explain: The order does not change the answer. 4 × 6 = 24.
steps: Order does not change the answer.
quiz.mistake: Works it out again and makes a slip

quiz.q: Rani sees 2 rows of 7 tiles. Which two sentences fit?
quiz.explain: 2 rows of 7 is 14. Turned around, 7 rows of 2 is also 14.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Which is true?
quiz.explain: Both are 15. The order does not matter in multiplication.
quiz.mistake: Thinks order changes the product

teach.ask: Gappu: Is 4 × 3 the same as 3 × 4?
teach.praise: Yes! Both are 12. Changing the order does not change the answer.
teach.nudge: What is 4 × 3? What is 3 × 4?

revise.summary: 4 groups of 3 and 3 groups of 4 both make 12. Changing the order in multiplication does not change the answer.
focus: Show that 4 × 3 = 3 × 4.
Write two × sentences for a picture of rows.
Use one fact to know its turn-around.
remember: Changing the order does not change the answer.
traps: Don't think a different order gives a different total.
Don't add the rows and the number in a row.

learn.hook: 8 packets of bindis, 5 in each. How many bindis? Multiply!
points: Same number in every packet? Multiply: packets × number in each.
8 packets of 5 bindis: 8 × 5 = 40 bindis.
4 shirts with 6 buttons each: 4 × 6 = 24 buttons.
6 pencils at ₹4 each cost 6 × 4 = ₹24.

example.q: 3 cars, with 4 people in each car. How many people?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers multiply to find the cost of many things with the same price.

quiz.q: Each packet has 5 bindis. How many bindis are in 8 packets?
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 and 5

quiz.q: A shirt has 6 buttons. How many buttons are on 4 shirts?
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 6

quiz.q: One pencil costs ₹4. How much do 6 pencils cost?
quiz.mistake: Adds the number of pencils and the price

quiz.q: 4 people sit in each car. How many people are in 3 cars?
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 4

quiz.q: A kite costs ₹10. Ravi buys 3 kites. How much does he pay?
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 10

quiz.q: Amma buys 2 boxes of 10 diyas each. How many diyas does she get?
quiz.mistake: Counts only one box

teach.ask: Gappu: One pencil costs ₹4. How do I find the cost of 6 pencils?
teach.nudge: Should I add 6 and 4 or multiply?

revise.summary: When every packet has the same number, multiply: packets × number in each. We also multiply to find the cost of many things with the same price.
focus: Solve packet and button stories with ×.
Find the cost of many things at the same price.
Solve people-in-cars stories.
remember: Total = packets × number in each.
8 × 5 = 40 bindis. 6 pencils at ₹4 each cost ₹24.
traps: Don't add the number of things and the price.
Don't add 8 and 5 for 8 packets of 5.
Count all the boxes, not just one.

learn.hook: Double the table of 2 and you get the table of 4. Magic!
points: The table of 4 is the table of 2 doubled: 3 × 2 = 6, so 3 × 4 = 12.
Double means add the number to itself: double 6 is 6 + 6 = 12.
Table of 8 = table of 2 + table of 6: 3 × 2 = 6 and 3 × 6 = 18, so 3 × 8 = 24.
An array has rows and columns. 3 rows of 5 dots: 3 × 5 = 15.

example.q: Find 5 × 4 by doubling.

learn.reallife: Eggs in a tray and chairs in a hall are set out in rows and columns.

quiz.q: 3 × 2 = 6. Double it to find 3 × 4.
quiz.explain: Double 6 is 6 + 6 = 12. So 3 × 4 = 12.
steps: Table of 4 = double the table of 2.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 instead of doubling

quiz.explain: Double 14 is 14 + 14 = 28.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 to 14

quiz.explain: Table of 8 = table of 2 + table of 6. 6 + 18 = 24.
quiz.mistake: Adds the wrong facts

quiz.q: A hall has 4 rows of chairs with 5 chairs in each row. How many chairs?
quiz.explain: 4 rows of 5 is 4 × 5 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds the rows and the chairs in a row

quiz.q: Which multiplication fits an array of 2 rows and 7 columns?
quiz.explain: 2 rows with 7 in each row is 2 × 7 = 14.
quiz.mistake: Adds the rows and columns

quiz.explain: 8 is double 4, so 5 × 8 is double 20. 20 + 20 = 40.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 to the answer

teach.ask: Gappu: How can I get the table of 4 from the table of 2?
teach.praise: Yes! Double each answer in the table of 2.
teach.nudge: What happens if I add each answer of the 2s table to itself?

revise.summary: The table of 4 is the table of 2 doubled, and the table of 8 is the table of 2 plus the table of 6. An array has rows and columns, so 3 rows of 5 is 3 × 5 = 15.
focus: Find facts of 4 by doubling facts of 2.
Find facts of 8 from facts of 2 and 6.
Write a × sentence for an array.
remember: Double means add the number to itself: double 6 is 12.
Table of 8 = table of 2 + table of 6.
traps: Don't add 2 instead of doubling.
Don't add the rows and the columns in an array.
To get 5 × 8 from 5 × 4, double 20. Don't add 4.

learn.hook: 6 laddoos and 2 friends. How do we share so it is fair?
points: Sharing equally means everyone gets the same.
Give one to each friend, again and again, till none are left.
12 shared by 3 friends: each gets 4.
Check by adding: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

example.q: Harpreet shares 10 bananas equally between 2 monkeys. How many does each get?
steps: Give 1 to each monkey. Keep going.
When all 10 are given, each monkey has 5.

learn.reallife: We share sweets on Diwali and split friends into equal teams for cricket.

quiz.q: Riya shares 8 laddoos equally with her brother. How many does each get?
quiz.explain: 8 shared by 2 people. 4 + 4 = 8, so each gets 4.
quiz.mistake: Takes 2 away from 8 instead of sharing

quiz.q: 15 pencils are shared equally by 3 children. How many does each child get?
quiz.explain: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15. So each child gets 5.
quiz.mistake: Takes 3 away from 15 instead of sharing

quiz.q: Kabir gives away all his 12 stickers, 3 to each friend. How many friends get stickers?
quiz.explain: Make groups of 3 till 12: 3, 6, 9, 12. That is 4 friends.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number each friend gets, not the number of friends

quiz.q: 20 children make 2 equal cricket teams. How many children are in each team?
quiz.explain: 10 + 10 = 20. So each team has 10 children.
quiz.mistake: Takes 2 away from 20 instead of sharing

quiz.q: Joseph shares 7 sweets equally between 2 friends. What happens?
options: Each gets 3 and 1 is left over
Each gets 3 and 2 are left over
quiz.explain: 3 + 3 = 6. One sweet is left. 4 + 4 = 8 is too many.
steps: Answer: Each gets 3 and 1 is left over
quiz.mistake: Thinks every number can be shared into 2 equal parts

quiz.q: Meena gets 4 balloons. Her 2 friends get 4 balloons each too. How many balloons were shared?
quiz.explain: Meena and 2 friends make 3 children. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to count Meena too

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I share 6 laddoos with my friend fairly?
teach.praise: Yes! Give one each again and again. We both get 3. Fair!
teach.nudge: Should we both get the same? How many does each of us get?

revise.summary: Sharing equally means everyone gets the same. Give one to each again and again till none are left, then check by adding.
focus: Share things equally and find how many each gets.
Find how many friends get a share.
Know when something is left over.
remember: 12 shared by 3 friends: each gets 4.
Check by adding: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
traps: Don't just take away 2 or 3. Share equally.
Not every number can be shared into 2 equal parts.
Don't forget to count yourself in the sharing.

learn.hook: 12 bindis and 2 ice-cream cone drawings to decorate. How many bindis on each?
points: To share equally, give one to each, again and again.
12 bindis on 2 cones: 6 on each.
2 plates with 6 laddoos each have 12 laddoos in all.
To put 12 laddoos on 3 plates equally, each plate gets 4.

example.q: Two plates have 6 laddoos each. Put them equally on 3 plates.

learn.reallife: At a birthday party, sweets are shared so everyone gets the same.

quiz.q: Sana draws 12 bindis equally on 2 ice-cream cones. How many on each cone?
quiz.explain: Share 12 between 2: 6 and 6. Check: 6 + 6 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 2 instead of sharing

quiz.q: Two plates have 6 laddoos each. How many laddoos in all?
quiz.explain: 6 + 6 = 12 laddoos.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one plate

quiz.q: 12 laddoos are put equally on 3 plates. How many on each plate?
quiz.explain: Give one to each plate again and again: 4, 4, 4. Check: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
steps: Share 12 on 3 plates, one at a time.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 3 instead of sharing

quiz.q: Two plates have 5 and 7 laddoos. Is this equal sharing?
quiz.explain: Equal sharing means every plate has the same number. 5 and 7 are not the same.
steps: Equal sharing: every plate has the same number.
So No, one plate has more.
Answer: No, one plate has more
quiz.mistake: Thinks any sharing is equal

quiz.q: Plates have 5 and 7 laddoos. How many should move from the 7-plate to make them equal?
quiz.explain: Move 1: then both plates have 6.
quiz.mistake: Moves the whole difference of 2

quiz.q: Kiran sticks 15 bindis equally on 3 cards. How many on each card?
quiz.explain: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15, so each card gets 5.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 3 instead of sharing

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I put 12 laddoos equally on 3 plates?
teach.praise: Yes! Give one to each plate again and again. Each plate gets 4.
teach.nudge: How can I make sure every plate gets the same?

revise.summary: To share equally with pictures, give one to each again and again. 2 plates of 6 laddoos is 12 in all, and 12 laddoos on 3 plates is 4 on each.
focus: Share a total on cones, plates or cards.
Find the total first, then share again.
Make unequal plates equal.
remember: 12 on 2 cones: 6 on each.
12 laddoos on 3 plates: 4 on each.
traps: Don't take away 2 or 3 instead of sharing.
Plates with 5 and 7 are not equal. Move 1, not 2.
Count both plates when finding the total.

topics.title: How many groups can we make?

learn.hook: 21 beads, 7 on each string. How many strings can you make?
points: To find how many groups, keep taking away one group till nothing is left.
21 beads, 7 on each string: 21 - 7 - 7 - 7 = 0. That is 3 strings.
To find how many in each group, share equally: 27 candles in 3 boxes is 9 in each.
Tables help: 3 × 7 = 21, so 21 beads make 3 strings of 7.

example.q: Rina has 20 flowers. She puts 5 in each vase. How many vases?

learn.reallife: A teacher makes teams of 5 from 30 children: 6 teams.

quiz.q: Tara has 21 beads. She puts 7 on each string. How many strings can she make?
quiz.explain: 21 - 7 = 14, 14 - 7 = 7, 7 - 7 = 0. She took 7 away 3 times.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 7 only once

quiz.q: Rina has 20 flowers. She puts 5 in each vase. How many vases does she need?
quiz.explain: Count in 5s to 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 vases.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number in each vase

quiz.q: 27 candles are packed equally in 3 boxes. How many candles are in each box?
quiz.explain: 9 + 9 + 9 = 27, so each box has 9.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 3 from 27

quiz.q: A shirt needs 6 buttons. How many shirts can 18 buttons go on?
quiz.explain: 6, 12, 18. That is 3 shirts.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 6 once and stops

quiz.q: Arun takes 4 marbles away from 12 again and again till none are left. How many times does he do it?
quiz.mistake: Gives what is left after the first take-away

quiz.q: 3 × 5 = 15. So 15 sweets in packets of 5 make how many packets?
quiz.explain: 3 packets of 5 make 15, so 15 sweets fill 3 packets.
quiz.mistake: Picks the number in each packet

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 21 beads and put 7 on each string. How many strings?
teach.praise: Yes! Take away 7 three times, so 3 strings. And 3 × 7 = 21!
teach.nudge: How many times can I take 7 away from 21?

revise.summary: To find how many groups, keep taking away one group till nothing is left. To find how many in each group, share equally.
focus: Find the number of groups by taking away again and again.
Find how many in each group by sharing.
Use tables to check.
remember: 27 candles in 3 boxes: 9 in each.
3 × 7 = 21, so 21 beads make 3 strings of 7.
traps: Don't take away the group only once and stop.
Don't give the number in each group when the number of groups is asked.
Don't give what is left after the first take-away.

learn.hook: Mangoes in summer, rain in the monsoon, sweaters in winter! India has many seasons.
points: We learn about five seasons: summer, rainy (monsoon), autumn, winter and spring.
Summer is hot. The rainy season brings lots of rain.
In autumn the weather turns pleasant and dry leaves fall. Winter is cold.
In spring, flowers bloom and new leaves grow.
Festivals come in different seasons: Holi in spring, Diwali in autumn, Lohri in winter.

example.q: Riya flies kites at Makar Sankranti in January. Which season is it?

learn.reallife: Summer vacation in May and June comes in the hottest part of the year.

quiz.q: Which season brings lots of rain?
quiz.explain: The monsoon is the rainy season in India.
steps: Each season has its own weather.
The monsoon brings lots of rain.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of seasons

quiz.q: In which season do flowers bloom and new leaves grow?
quiz.explain: Spring is the season of new flowers and leaves.
steps: New flowers and leaves grow in spring.
Winter is cold; rainy season is wet.
quiz.mistake: Thinks flowers bloom most in winter

quiz.q: Holi is the festival of colours. In which season do we play Holi?
quiz.explain: Holi comes in March, in spring.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the festival to its season

quiz.q: Lohri is celebrated with a bonfire in January. Which season is it?
quiz.explain: January is cold, so it is winter. People sit around the warm fire.
quiz.mistake: Does not link January with winter

quiz.q: Kabir drinks lots of water and eats mangoes during his vacation. Which season is it?
quiz.explain: Mangoes and hot days mean summer.
steps: Mangoes and hot days come together.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up summer and rainy season

quiz.q: In which season does the weather turn pleasant and Diwali come?
quiz.explain: Diwali comes in October or November, in autumn.
steps: Diwali comes in October or November.
The weather turns pleasant then: autumn.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the autumn season

teach.ask: Gappu: What are the seasons in India?
teach.praise: Wow! Summer, rainy, autumn, winter and spring. Each one is special!
teach.nudge: Which season is hot? Which one brings rain?

revise.summary: We learn about five seasons: summer, rainy (monsoon), autumn, winter and spring. Festivals come in different seasons, like Holi in spring, Diwali in autumn and Lohri in winter.
focus: Name the five seasons and what each is like.
Link a festival to its season.
Use clues in a story to find the season.
remember: Seasons: summer, rainy (monsoon), autumn, winter, spring.
Holi: spring. Diwali: autumn. Lohri: winter.
traps: Flowers bloom in spring, not in winter.
Don't mix up summer and the rainy season.
January is winter.

learn.hook: Mangoes, umbrellas and sweaters! Each one belongs to a season.
points: In summer it is hot. We drink cool water and eat mangoes.
In the rainy season it rains a lot. We use umbrellas and raincoats.
In winter it is cold. We wear sweaters.
A calendar shows the days, weeks and months of a year.
Most months have 30 or 31 days. February is the shortest month.

example.q: On a calendar, the 1st of the month is a Monday. What day is the 8th?
steps: So the 8th is also a Monday.

learn.reallife: We look at the calendar to find festivals, holidays and birthdays.

games.title: True or false?
items: Winter is cold, so we wear warm clothes.
A calendar shows the days and months.
It shows every day of every month.
We use umbrellas in the rainy season.
Umbrellas keep us dry in the rain.
If the 1st is a Monday, the 8th is a Monday too.
7 days later it is the same day again.
Summer is hot. Winter is the cold one.

quiz.q: In which season do we wear sweaters?
quiz.explain: Winter is cold. Sweaters keep us warm.
steps: We need them when it is cold.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up hot and cold seasons

quiz.q: Aisha carries an umbrella and makes paper boats in puddles. Which season is it?
quiz.explain: Puddles and umbrellas mean lots of rain. It is the rainy season.
steps: Umbrella and puddles mean lots of rain.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the clues in the story

quiz.q: On a calendar, the 1st is a Friday. What day is the 8th?
quiz.explain: The 8th is 7 days after the 1st. 7 days later is the same day: Friday.
steps: 7 days later is the same day
quiz.mistake: Moves on 1 day instead of 7 days

quiz.q: On a calendar, the 5th is a Tuesday. On which date is the next Tuesday?
quiz.explain: The next Tuesday is 7 days later. 5 + 7 = 12.
steps: The same day comes again after 7 days.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 days instead of 7, or adds 1

quiz.q: Most months have how many days?
quiz.explain: Most months have 30 or 31 days. Only February has fewer.
steps: Months are longer than a week.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up days in a month with days in a week or months in a year

quiz.q: Which month is the shortest?
quiz.explain: February has only 28 days, or 29 in a leap year. Other months have 30 or 31.
steps: February has 28 days (29 in a leap year).
quiz.mistake: Thinks all months have the same number of days

teach.ask: Gappu: What do we wear and do in each season?
teach.praise: Lovely! Mangoes in summer, umbrellas in the rain, sweaters in winter!
teach.nudge: What happens in summer? In the rainy season? In winter?

revise.summary: Summer is hot, the rainy season brings lots of rain and winter is cold. A calendar shows the days, weeks and months of a year.
focus: Use clues to name the season.
Find the same day of the week 7 days later.
Know how many days most months have.
remember: Most months have 30 or 31 days. February is the shortest month.
7 days later is the same day of the week.
traps: Don't move on 1 day to find the same day next week. Move on 7.
Not all months have the same number of days.
Don't mix up days in a month with days in a week.

learn.hook: Birthdays, Diwali and summer holidays! They all come in different months.
points: A year has 12 months.
January, February, March, April, May, June.
July, August, September, October, November, December.
January is the first month. December is the last month.
After December, a new year starts with January.

example.q: Which month comes just after March? Which comes just before March?
steps: The month after March is April.
The month before March is February.
example.answer: April comes after. February comes before.

learn.reallife: A calendar on the wall has one page for each of the 12 months.

quiz.q: How many months are there in a year?
quiz.explain: January to December makes 12 months.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up months in a year with days in a week

quiz.q: Which month comes just after June?
quiz.explain: The order is May, June, July. So July comes after June.
quiz.mistake: Gives the month before, or skips a month

quiz.q: Which is the first month of the year?
quiz.explain: Every year starts with January.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the first and the last month

quiz.q: Which month comes just before January?
quiz.explain: December is the last month. Then a new year starts with January.
steps: December is the last month of the year.
Then a new year starts with January.
quiz.mistake: Thinks nothing comes before January

quiz.q: Meena's birthday is in the 3rd month of the year. Which month is it?
quiz.explain: 1st January, 2nd February, 3rd March.
quiz.mistake: Counts from the wrong month

quiz.q: How many months come after September in the same year?
quiz.explain: After September come October, November and December. That is 3 months.
quiz.mistake: Counts September too

teach.ask: Gappu: How many months are in a year? Which one comes first?
teach.praise: Hooray! 12 months, and January comes first. December is last!
teach.nudge: How many months are there? What is the name of the first one?

revise.summary: A year has 12 months, from January to December. January is the first month and December is the last; after December, a new year starts with January.
focus: Say the 12 months in order.
Find the month just before or just after.
Find a month from its place, like the 3rd month.
remember: A year has 12 months.
January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December.
traps: December comes just before January.
Don't count September when asked how many months come after it.
Don't mix up the first and the last month.

topics.title: How many days in each month?

points: Months have 30 or 31 days, except February.
30 days: April, June, September and November.
31 days: January, March, May, July, August, October and December.
February has 28 days, but 29 days in a leap year.
A leap year comes once in 4 years, like 2024 and 2028.

example.q: How many days are in July and in September?

learn.reallife: Knuckle trick: make two fists. Months on knuckles have 31 days. Months in the dips have fewer.

games.title: True or false?
items: February has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year
A leap year comes every year
July and August both have 31 days.

quiz.q: How many days are there in April?
quiz.explain: April is one of the 30-day months: April, June, September, November.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every month has 31 days

quiz.q: How many days are there in December?
quiz.explain: December has 31 days.
steps: December is not in the list, and it is not February.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 30-day and 31-day months

quiz.q: How many days does February have in a leap year?
quiz.explain: February has 28 days, and 1 more in a leap year: 29.
steps: In a leap year it gets 1 more.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the extra day of a leap year

quiz.q: How often does a leap year come?
quiz.explain: A leap year comes once every 4 years.
steps: A leap year does not come every year.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every year is a leap year

quiz.q: 2024 was a leap year. Which year is the next leap year?
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 year instead of 4

quiz.q: Which of these months has 30 days?
quiz.explain: September is a 30-day month. The others have 31 days.
quiz.mistake: Does not remember the 30-day months

teach.ask: Gappu: Do all months have the same number of days?
teach.praise: Right! Most have 30 or 31, and February has 28 or 29.
teach.nudge: Which month is different from all the rest?

revise.summary: Months have 30 or 31 days, except February. February has 28 days, but 29 days in a leap year, which comes once in 4 years.
focus: Know the 30-day and 31-day months.
Know February's days in a normal and a leap year.
Find the next leap year.
remember: 30 days: April, June, September, November.
31 days: January, March, May, July, August, October, December.
February: 28 days, 29 in a leap year. A leap year comes once in 4 years.
traps: Not every month has 31 days.
Not every year is a leap year.
The next leap year after 2024 is 2028, not 2025.

learn.hook: Sunday is fun day! But which day comes after it? Let's learn the 7 days.
points: A week has 7 days.
Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.
After Saturday, a new week starts with Sunday.
Yesterday is the day before today. Tomorrow is the day after today.

example.q: Today is Wednesday. What day will it be tomorrow? What day was it yesterday?
steps: The day after Wednesday is Thursday.
The day before Wednesday is Tuesday.
example.answer: Tomorrow is Thursday. Yesterday was Tuesday.

learn.reallife: School days, the weekly market day and the Sunday holiday all follow the days of the week.

quiz.q: How many days are there in a week?
quiz.explain: Sunday to Saturday makes 7 days.
steps: Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat
quiz.mistake: Counts only the school days

quiz.q: Today is Thursday. What day is tomorrow?
quiz.explain: Tomorrow is the day after today. After Thursday comes Friday.
quiz.mistake: Gives the day before instead of the day after

quiz.q: Yesterday was Sunday. What day is today?

Choose balloons that make an exact amount.
Find the most you can win with some chances.

Check your choice by adding again.

learn.hook: ₹66 for a storybook. Which notes and coins will you give?

To use the fewest notes and coins, start with the biggest one that fits.
Keep taking the biggest that fits till the amount is made.

example.q: Pay ₹38 with the fewest notes and coins.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers try to give change with as few coins as they can.

games.title: True or false?
items: There is only one way to make ₹20
A ₹20 note, two ₹10s, four ₹5s and more.
To use the fewest notes, start with the biggest that fits
Big notes cover more of the amount.
Two ₹20 notes and one ₹10 note make ₹50

quiz.mistake: Does not add all the notes and coins

quiz.mistake: Does not add the given notes first

quiz.mistake: Uses three ₹10 notes

quiz.explain: All three make ₹38. The second set uses only 5 pieces; the other two use 6.

quiz.mistake: Does not start with the biggest note

quiz.explain: 45 - 5 = 40, and 40 is two ₹20 notes.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ₹5 coin

quiz.q: Which is the fewest notes to pay ₹150?
quiz.explain: ₹100 + ₹50 uses just 2 notes.
quiz.mistake: Does not start with the biggest note

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to pay ₹38 with as few notes and coins as I can. How?

teach.nudge: Which note should I start with?

revise.summary: An amount can be made in many ways, like ₹66 = ₹50 + ₹10 + ₹5 + ₹1. To use the fewest notes and coins, keep taking the biggest one that fits.
focus: Check which set makes an amount.
Find a missing note or coin.
Pay with the fewest notes and coins.
remember: Fewest notes and coins: start with the biggest one that fits.

Add the given notes before finding what is missing.
Don't forget the ₹5 coin when working back.

learn.hook: You give the shopkeeper ₹20 for a ₹15 toy. Do you get money back?
points: The shopkeeper sells. We buy and pay.
If we pay more than the price, the shopkeeper gives money back. This is called change.
Change = money we give − price.
Pay ₹20 for a ₹15 toy: change is ₹5.

example.q: Meena buys a ribbon for ₹12. She pays with a ₹20 note. How much change does she get?

learn.reallife: At the fair, the vegetable market or the school canteen, we pay and get change.

games.title: True or false?
items: If you pay ₹10 for a ₹10 toffee packet, you get no change.
Paying ₹50 for a ₹30 book gives ₹20 change.
Paying ₹20 for a ₹14 pen gives ₹4 change.
With only ₹10 you can buy a toy that costs ₹25.
₹25 is more than ₹10. You need ₹15 more.
The shopkeeper gives change when we pay more than the price.
Change is the extra money given back.

quiz.q: A kite costs ₹15. Arjun pays ₹20. How much change does he get?
quiz.explain: Change = ₹20 − ₹15. Count up from 15 to 20: that is 5. So ₹5.
quiz.mistake: Adds the money and the price

quiz.q: Aisha has ₹30. A doll costs ₹25. Can she buy it?
quiz.explain: ₹30 is more than ₹25, so she can buy it. ₹30 − ₹25 = ₹5 change.
steps: Answer: Yes, and she gets ₹5 back
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the money with the price

quiz.q: Kabir pays ₹50 for a toy car that costs ₹35. How much change does he get?
quiz.mistake: Does 5 − 0 in the ones instead of breaking a ten

quiz.q: Joseph has ₹40. He buys a ball for ₹18. How much money is left?
quiz.mistake: Does 8 − 0 in the ones, or forgets that one ten was broken

quiz.q: A stall sells laddoos at ₹5 each. How much for 4 laddoos?
quiz.explain: 4 laddoos at ₹5 each. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. So ₹20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 5 instead of counting ₹5 four times

quiz.q: Riya wants a ₹60 bag. She has ₹45. How much more money does she need?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two amounts, or does 5 − 0 in the ones

teach.ask: Gappu: I pay ₹20 for a ₹15 toy. How much change do I get?
teach.praise: Yes! ₹20 take away ₹15 is ₹5. I get ₹5 back!
teach.nudge: How much more is ₹20 than ₹15? Should I take away?

revise.summary: The shopkeeper sells and we buy and pay. If we pay more than the price, the money we get back is called change: change = money we give − price.
focus: Find the change.
Tell if there is enough money to buy something.
Find how much more money is needed.
remember: Change = money we give − price.
Pay ₹20 for a ₹15 toy: change is ₹5.
traps: Don't add the money and the price to find change.
Don't do 5 − 0 in ₹50 − ₹35. Break a ten.
Don't add 4 and 5 for 4 laddoos at ₹5.

learn.hook: On Colour Day, everyone wears a favourite colour. Let us count!
points: Count the children for each colour and write the number in a table.
The colour with the biggest number is the most liked.
The colour with the smallest number is the least liked.
Compare two rows using more than, less than or equal to.

example.q: Colour table: Red 7, Blue 4, Green 5, Yellow 2. Which is most liked and which is least liked?
steps: The biggest number is 7, for red.
The smallest number is 2, for yellow.
example.answer: Red is most liked; yellow is least liked

learn.reallife: Teachers make tables of how many children take the school bus each day.

items.text: 3 guavas and 3 mangoes: guavas are ___ mangoes

games.title: True or false?
items: If 7 children wear red and 4 wear blue, red is liked more
The least liked colour has the biggest number
If green has 5 and yellow has 2, yellow is liked more
A table helps us see the numbers clearly

quiz.q: Colour Day table: Red 7, Blue 4, Green 5, Yellow 2. Which colour is most liked?
quiz.explain: Red has the biggest number, 7.
quiz.mistake: Picks the smallest number

quiz.q: In the table Red 7, Blue 4, Green 5, Yellow 2, which colour is least liked?
quiz.explain: Yellow has the smallest number, 2.
quiz.mistake: Picks the biggest number

quiz.explain: 7 - 4 = 3 more.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the difference

quiz.mistake: Mixes up more than and less than

teach.praise: Yes! The colour with the biggest number is the most liked.
teach.nudge: Which number in the table should I look for?

revise.summary: Count the children for each colour and write the number in a table. The biggest number is the most liked and the smallest number is the least liked.
focus: Find the most liked and least liked from a table.
Compare two rows with more than, less than or equal to.
Find how many in all or how many more.

Don't leave out a row when adding.
Two rows with the same number are equal.

learn.hook: Which sweet does your class like best? Let's ask and find out!
points: Data is information we collect, like the favourite fruits of our friends.
We ask a question and write down the answers.
We sort things into groups by colour, shape or kind.
Then we count each group and compare.

example.q: Riya asks 8 friends their favourite sweet. 5 say laddoo and 3 say jalebi. Which is liked more?

learn.reallife: Teachers count how many children are present. Shopkeepers count which toys sell the most.

games.title: True or false?
items: We can sort buttons by colour.
Red buttons in one group, blue in another.
Data is a kind of food.
Data is information we collect, like answers or counts.
After sorting, we count each group.
Counting tells us how many are in each group.
If 6 children like tea and 4 like milk, more children like milk.
6 is more than 4, so more children like tea.
Asking friends their favourite game is collecting data.

quiz.q: Arjun sorts 10 marbles. 6 are red and the rest are blue. How many are blue?
quiz.explain: The rest means what is left. 10 − 6 = 4 blue marbles.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the rest

quiz.q: In a class, 7 children like cricket and 5 like football. How many children in all?
quiz.explain: 'In all' means add. 7 + 5 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: 7 children like cricket and 5 like football. How many more children like cricket?
quiz.explain: 'How many more' means find the difference. 7 − 5 = 2.
steps: 'How many more' means find the difference.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two groups instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Meena puts her red toys in one box and her blue toys in another. What is she doing?
quiz.explain: Putting things into groups by colour is sorting.
steps: Red toys in one box, blue in another.
Putting things into groups is sorting.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word for making groups

quiz.q: Kabir asks 9 friends. 4 like mango, 3 like apple and 2 like banana. Which fruit is liked the least?
quiz.explain: Banana has only 2. That is the smallest number.
quiz.mistake: Picks the fruit liked the most

quiz.q: Aisha has 3 red, 5 yellow and 4 green bangles. How many bangles in all?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one colour

teach.ask: Gappu: My friends told me their favourite fruits. What do I do now?
teach.praise: Great! Sort the answers into groups and count each group. Now I know the favourite!
teach.nudge: Should I put the same answers together? Then what do I do with each group?

revise.summary: Data is information we collect, like the favourite fruits of our friends. We ask a question, write down the answers, sort them into groups, then count and compare.
focus: Know what data and sorting mean.
Find 'in all', 'how many more' and 'the rest'.
Find which is liked most or least.
remember: Data is information we collect.
Putting things into groups by colour, shape or kind is sorting.
traps: 'In all' means add. 'How many more' means find the difference.
'The rest' means what is left, so take away.
Don't leave out a group when adding.

learn.hook: Cars zoom past the school gate. How can we keep count fast? Tally marks!
points: Make one small line | for each thing you count.
For the 5th thing, draw a line across the first 4 lines. This makes a bundle of 5.
Count the bundles by 5s. Then add the extra lines.
Tally marks help us count while things keep coming.

example.q: Kabir counts cars with tally marks. He has 2 bundles and 3 more lines. How many cars?

learn.reallife: In a cricket match, scorers can use tally marks to keep count of runs.

quiz.q: Kabir counts cars at the gate. His tally is |||. How many cars?
quiz.explain: Each line is 1. There are 3 lines, so the number is 3.
quiz.mistake: Miscounts the lines

quiz.q: How do we make a bundle of 5 in tally marks?
options: We draw a line across 4 lines
quiz.explain: We draw 4 lines. The 5th line goes across them. That is a bundle of 5.
steps: Answer: We draw a line across 4 lines
quiz.mistake: Does not know how the 5th tally mark is drawn

quiz.q: Riya's tally shows 3 bundles. How many is that?
quiz.explain: Each bundle is 5. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15.
quiz.mistake: Counts bundles as 1 each, or adds 3 and 5

quiz.q: Joseph's tally shows 2 bundles and |||| (4 lines). How many is that?
quiz.explain: 2 bundles: 5, 10. Then 4 more: 11, 12, 13, 14.
quiz.mistake: Counts each bundle as 1, or writes 2 and 4 side by side

quiz.q: How do we show 7 with tally marks?
quiz.explain: 1 bundle is 5. 5 and 2 more make 7. So 1 bundle and ||.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each bundle is 1, or adds one line too many

quiz.q: Aisha's bird tally shows 1 bundle and |. Then 3 more birds come. How many birds now?

quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the new birds, or counts the bundle as 1

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I make tally marks for 5?
teach.praise: Yes! Draw 4 lines, then the 5th line goes across. A bundle of 5!
teach.nudge: How many lines do I draw first? Where does the 5th line go?

revise.summary: Tally marks are small lines, one for each thing counted. For the 5th thing, draw a line across the first 4 to make a bundle of 5, then count bundles by 5s and add the extra lines.
focus: Read a tally of bundles and lines.
Show a number with tally marks.
Add new things to a tally.
remember: One line | for each thing.
The 5th line goes across the first 4: a bundle of 5.
traps: A bundle is 5, not 1.
Don't write 2 and 4 side by side for 2 bundles and 4 lines. It is 14.
Don't forget to add the new things that come.

topics.title: Drawing a pictograph: travel to school

learn.hook: How do you come to school? Bus, cycle, walk or car? Let us make a picture graph!
points: First fill a table: how many children come each way.
In a pictograph, draw one face 🙂 for each child.
Put the faces in rows, one row for each way of travel.
Make every face the same size and keep the rows neat, so we can compare.

example.q: Table: Bus 5, Walk 3, Cycle 4, Car 2. How many faces go in the Cycle row?

learn.reallife: School notice boards often show picture graphs.

games.title: Rows by length
games.prompt: Rows from fewest faces to most

quiz.q: Table: Bus 5, Walk 3, Cycle 4, Car 2. How many children were asked?

quiz.mistake: Draws before collecting the data

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I draw a pictograph of how children come to school?
teach.praise: Yes! One face for each child, in a row for each way of travel.

revise.summary: To draw a pictograph, first fill a table, then draw one face 🙂 for each child in a row for each way of travel. All faces should be the same size so we can compare.
focus: Draw the right number of faces in each row.
Read and compare rows of a pictograph.
Know the order: table first, then pictograph.
remember: One face for each child.
Make every face the same size and keep the rows neat.
traps: Don't draw one face for the whole row.
The size of the pictures does matter. Keep them the same.
Don't draw before collecting the data.

learn.hook: A graph made of pictures! Let's read a pictograph.

Count the pictures in each row.

learn.hook: Kho-kho, kabaddi or cricket? Which game does your class love most?
points: Ask each child their favourite game and count.
Fill a table, then draw a face chart with one face for each child.
The longest row shows the most liked game. The shortest row shows the least liked.
Compare games: how many more like one game than another.

example.q: Cricket 8, Kho-kho 5, Kabaddi 3. How many more children like cricket than kabaddi?

learn.reallife: Sports teachers ask which games children like before planning Sports Day.

games.title: True or false?
items: The longest row in a face chart shows the most liked game
If kho-kho has 5 faces and kabaddi 3, kabaddi is liked more
5 is more than 3, so kho-kho is liked more.
Each face stands for one child
We find the total by adding all the rows
Add every row to count all the children.
The shortest row shows the most liked game
The shortest row is the least liked.

items.q: Cricket 8, Kabaddi 3: how many more like cricket
Football 7, Cricket 8: how many more like cricket

quiz.q: Face chart: Cricket 8, Kho-kho 5, Kabaddi 3, Football 6. Which game is liked the least?

quiz.mistake: Picks the longest row

quiz.q: 6 children like football and 3 like kabaddi. How many more like football?
quiz.explain: 6 - 3 = 3 more.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers

quiz.q: 8 children chose cricket and 5 chose kho-kho. How many chose these two games in all?

quiz.q: Kabaddi has 🙂🙂🙂🙂 and kho-kho has 🙂🙂🙂🙂. Which is true?

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find the most liked game from a face chart?

teach.nudge: Which row should I look at?

revise.summary: Ask each child their favourite game, fill a table and draw a face chart with one face for each child. The longest row is the most liked game and the shortest row is the least liked.
focus: Find the most and least liked game.
Compare two games: how many more.
Add two rows.
remember: One face for each child.
Longest row = most liked. Shortest row = least liked.
traps: Don't pick the shortest row for most liked.
Two rows can be equal.
Don't count a row as one.

learn.hook: Be a survey star! Ask your friends a question and write down the answers.
points: A survey means asking many people the same question.
Write the answers in a table using tally marks or numbers.
Use the table to answer questions, like which vegetable is most liked.
We can also ask friends how many people are in their family.
Then find the most common family size and count families bigger than a given size.

example.q: Family sizes of 6 friends: 4, 3, 5, 4, 6, 4. Which family size is the most common?

learn.reallife: Schools sometimes ask parents questions to plan a picnic.

items.text: Family sizes 3, 5, 4, 4: the smallest family has ___
Sizes 4, 3, 5, 4, 6, 4: the most common size is ___
Sizes 4, 3, 5, 6: families with more than 4 members: ___

quiz.q: Vegetable survey: Potato 9, Carrot 4, Peas 6, Bhindi 5. Which is the most liked?
quiz.explain: Potato has the biggest number, 9.
quiz.mistake: Picks the smallest number

quiz.q: Vegetable survey: Potato 9, Carrot 4, Peas 6, Bhindi 5. How many children were asked in all?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one row

quiz.q: Family sizes of friends: 4, 3, 5, 4, 6, 4. Which family size is the most common?
quiz.explain: 4 comes three times. The others come once.
quiz.mistake: Picks the biggest family instead

quiz.q: Family sizes: 4, 3, 5, 4, 6, 4. How many members does the smallest family have?
quiz.explain: The smallest number in the list is 3.
quiz.mistake: Picks the most common size

quiz.q: Family sizes: 4, 3, 5, 4, 6, 4. How many families have more than 4 members?
quiz.explain: Only 5 and 6 are more than 4. That is 2 families.
quiz.mistake: Counts the families of 4 too

quiz.q: What is a survey?
options: Asking many people the same question
quiz.explain: In a survey we ask many people one question and record their answers.
steps: Answer: Asking many people the same question
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a survey is

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find my friends' favourite vegetable?
teach.praise: Great! Ask everyone, write the answers in a table and count.
teach.nudge: What should I do first? Where do I write the answers?

revise.summary: A survey means asking many people the same question and writing the answers in a table. We use the table to answer questions, like the most liked vegetable or the most common family size.
focus: Know what a survey is.
Answer questions from a survey table.
Find the most common family size and count bigger families.
remember: A survey means asking many people the same question.
Write the answers using tally marks or numbers.
traps: The most common size is not the biggest family.
'More than 4' does not include families of 4.
Don't leave out a row when adding.

learn.hook: Who lives with Dada-Dadi or Nana-Nani? Let us plan a family survey!
points: Plan your questions before the survey: what do you want to find out?
Good survey questions are short and clear, like 'Do your grandparents live with you?'
Visit families and write each answer in a table.
Sort families into: both grandparents, one grandparent, or no grandparents at home.

example.q: Table: Both 4, One 3, None 5. How many families were asked?

learn.reallife: Grandparents share stories, festivals and recipes with the family.

games.title: Survey question or not?
items: Do your grandparents live with you?
How many people are in your family?

items.q: Both 6, None 2: how many more Both

quiz.q: What should you do before you start a survey?
quiz.explain: Planning the questions tells you what to ask and what to record.
quiz.mistake: Starts without a plan

quiz.q: Which is a clear survey question?
options: Do your grandparents live with you?
quiz.explain: It is short and has a clear answer.
steps: A survey question must be clear.
'Do your grandparents live with you?' is short with a clear answer.
Answer: Do your grandparents live with you?
quiz.mistake: Picks an unclear question

quiz.q: Table: Both 4, One 3, None 5. How many families have no grandparents at home?
quiz.explain: The None row shows 5.
quiz.mistake: Reads the wrong row

quiz.q: Table: Both 4, One 3, None 5. How many families were asked in all?
quiz.mistake: Adds only two rows

quiz.q: Table: Both 4, One 3, None 5. How many families have one or both grandparents at home?
quiz.explain: Both 4 + One 3 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the Both row

quiz.q: Table: Both 6, One 2, None 1. Which group is the biggest?
quiz.explain: 6 is the biggest number.
quiz.mistake: Picks the smallest number

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to know how many families live with grandparents. What do I do?
teach.praise: Yes! Plan a clear question, ask each family and record the answers in a table.
teach.nudge: What should I ask? Where do I write the answers?

revise.summary: Plan your questions before a survey. Good questions are short and clear; write each answer in a table and sort families into both, one or no grandparents at home.
focus: Plan before the survey.
Choose a clear survey question.
Read and add rows of the table.
remember: Plan your questions before the survey.
Good survey questions are short and clear.
traps: Don't start without a plan.
Don't add only two rows when all are asked.
'One or both' means add the One and Both rows.

learn.hook: Puzzle time! Find the shadow, solve the riddle and move the matchsticks.
points: In a 'join the pairs' puzzle, join each shape to its match without any lines crossing.
A ball makes a circle shadow. A party cap seen from the side makes a triangle shadow.
Shape riddles: 'I have 3 sides and 3 corners' is a triangle.
4 matchsticks make 1 square. 12 sticks can make a big square with 4 small squares inside.

example.q: 12 matchsticks make a big square with 4 small squares inside. Remove the 4 sticks inside. How many squares are left?
steps: The 4 inside sticks make the cross in the middle.
Without them, only the outside is left.

learn.reallife: Puzzle pages in children's magazines have riddles and matchstick puzzles.

games.title: Who am I?
pairs: I am round and flat with no corners
I roll and have no flat face

games.title: True or false?
items: In a join-the-pairs puzzle, the lines should not cross
The puzzle is to join every pair without lines crossing.
A ball makes a circle shadow
A ball looks round from every side.
A dice makes a triangle shadow
A dice face makes a square shadow.
2 squares that share a side need 8 matchsticks
They share one stick, so they need 7.

quiz.q: I have 3 sides and 3 corners. Who am I?
quiz.explain: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the number of sides

quiz.q: I have no corners and no edges, and I can roll. Who am I?
quiz.explain: A sphere is curved all over, so it has no corners or edges.
steps: No corners, no edges, can roll.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cone has no corners

quiz.q: Which object can make a circle shadow?
options: A party cap seen from the side
quiz.explain: A ball is round from every side, so its shadow is a circle.
steps: A circle shadow needs a round object.
A ball is round from every side.
quiz.mistake: Picks an object with straight edges

quiz.q: How many matchsticks do you need to make 2 squares that do not touch?
quiz.explain: Each square needs 4 sticks. 4 + 4 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Thinks they share a stick

quiz.q: Two squares share one side. How many matchsticks are needed?
quiz.explain: 8 sticks for two squares, but one side is shared. 8 - 1 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the shared stick

quiz.q: A big square of 12 matchsticks has 4 small squares inside. Take away the 4 inside sticks. How many squares are left?
quiz.explain: Only the outside is left, and it is 1 big square.
steps: Only the outside sticks are left.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the small squares are still there

quiz.q: In a join-the-pairs puzzle, you join each shape to its matching shape. What must be true about the lines?
options: They must all cross in the middle
They must not cross each other
quiz.explain: The puzzle is to join every pair so that no two lines cross.
steps: Join each shape to its match.
The rule: no two lines cross.
Answer: They must not cross each other
quiz.mistake: Thinks any way of joining is fine, even with crossing lines

teach.ask: Gappu: Give me a riddle for a triangle!
teach.praise: Great riddle! I have 3 sides and 3 corners. I am a triangle!
teach.nudge: How many sides and corners does a triangle have?

revise.summary: Shape puzzles use what we know about shapes. Riddles give sides and corners, shadows show flat shapes, and 4 matchsticks make 1 square.
focus: Solve shape riddles.
Count matchsticks for squares.
Join pairs without crossing lines.
remember: 3 sides and 3 corners: a triangle.
A ball makes a circle shadow.
4 matchsticks make 1 square.
traps: Two squares that share a side need 7 sticks, not 8.
Lines in a join-the-pairs puzzle must not cross.
A sphere has no corners and no edges.

topics.title: Patterns, number names and same-digit numbers

learn.hook: Eleven, twelve, thir-teen! Let us spell numbers and finish patterns.
points: Number names 11 to 20: eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty.
To complete a pattern, find what repeats or how much is added each time.
Using one digit twice makes numbers like 11, 22, 33 ... 99.
There are 9 such 2-digit numbers.

example.q: What comes next: 11, 22, 33, ?

learn.reallife: We read number names in storybooks and on signboards.

quiz.q: How do we write 17 in words?
quiz.explain: 17 is seven more than ten: seventeen.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up seventeen and seventy

quiz.q: Which number is 'nineteen'?
quiz.explain: Nineteen is 1 ten and 9 ones: 19.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up nineteen and ninety

quiz.q: Complete the pattern: 11, 22, 33, ___
quiz.explain: Each number adds 11. 33 + 11 = 44.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 11

quiz.q: Using only the digit 8, which 2-digit number can you make?
quiz.explain: Put 8 in both places: 88.
quiz.mistake: Uses another digit too

quiz.q: How many 2-digit numbers have both digits the same, like 11 and 22?
steps: One for each digit 1 to 9 (00 is not 2-digit).
quiz.mistake: Counts 00 or 100 too

quiz.q: Complete the pattern: 2, 4, 6, ___, 10
quiz.explain: The pattern adds 2. 6 + 2 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 2

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I say the numbers from 11 to 15?
teach.praise: Yes! Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen.
teach.nudge: What comes after ten? Can you say the teen numbers?

revise.summary: Number names 11 to 20 are eleven to twenty. To complete a pattern, find what repeats or how much is added, and using one digit twice gives 9 numbers: 11, 22 ... 99.
focus: Read and write number names 11 to 20.
Complete patterns.
Know the 2-digit numbers with the same digit twice.
remember: Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty.
There are 9 numbers like 11, 22, 33 ... 99.
traps: Don't mix up seventeen and seventy, or nineteen and ninety.
Don't add 1 when the pattern adds 11.
Don't count 00 or 100.

learn.hook: Think of a number ... I know your answer! It is always 4!
points: Trick: think of a number, double it, add 8, take half, then take away the number you thought of. The answer is always 4!
Double means 2 times. Half means splitting into 2 equal parts.
Double 9 is 18, so half of 18 is 9.
On a calculator, press keys to make a number: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20.

example.q: Try the trick with 3.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers use calculators to add bills quickly.

quiz.q: Which number has a double of 18?
quiz.explain: Double 9 is 9 + 9 = 18. So the number is 9, half of 18.
steps: Double means add the number to itself.
quiz.mistake: Doubles 18 instead of halving

quiz.q: Try the trick with 5: double it (10), add 8 (18), take half (9), take away 5. What do you get?
quiz.explain: 9 - 5 = 4. The trick always ends in 4!
quiz.mistake: Stops before the last step

quiz.q: Do the trick with 7. What is the final answer?
quiz.explain: Double 7 = 14, add 8 = 22, half = 11, take away 7 = 4.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to take away the starting number

quiz.q: Using only the keys 5, + and =, how many times must you press 5 to make 20?
quiz.explain: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20. That is 4 fives.
quiz.mistake: Counts the plus signs instead

quiz.q: Using only the keys 2, + and =, which number can you NOT make?
quiz.explain: Adding 2s gives 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 ... only even numbers. 7 is odd.
steps: 7 is odd, so we cannot make 7.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that adding 2s gives even numbers

quiz.q: What is half of 14?
quiz.explain: 7 + 7 = 14, so half of 14 is 7.
quiz.mistake: Doubles instead of halving

teach.ask: Gappu: What is the double of 9, and what is half of 18?
teach.praise: Yes! Double 9 is 18, and half of 18 is 9.
teach.nudge: What do I get if I add 9 and 9?

revise.summary: Think of a number, double it, add 8, take half and take away your number: the answer is always 4. Double means 2 times and half means splitting into 2 equal parts.
focus: Do the number trick step by step.
Find doubles and halves.
Make numbers on a calculator with one key.
remember: Double 9 is 18, so half of 18 is 9.
The trick always ends in 4.
traps: Don't stop before the last step: take away your number.
Don't double when half is asked.
Adding only 2s gives even numbers, so you cannot make 7.

topics.title: Sums, signs and the star puzzle

learn.hook: Pick numbers that add to 30, choose + or -, and balance the star!
points: To make a total like 30, try pairs: 10 + 20, 25 + 5, 15 + 15.
To fill + or -, try each sign: 12 ___ 5 = 7 needs -, because 12 - 5 = 7.
If the answer is bigger than the first number, use +. If it is smaller, use -.
Star puzzle: put 1 to 7 on 3 lines that share the middle. With 4 in the middle, pair 1 and 7, 2 and 6, 3 and 5. Each line adds to 12.
learn.reallife: Cashiers decide to add or take away when they count money.

quiz.q: Which two numbers add up to 30?
quiz.explain: 18 + 12 = 30. The others make 25, 32 and 25.
quiz.mistake: Does not add to check

quiz.explain: 7 is smaller than 12, so take away: 12 - 5 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Always picks +

quiz.explain: 14 is bigger than 8, so add: 8 + 6 = 14.
quiz.mistake: Always picks -

quiz.q: From 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25, which three numbers add to 30?
quiz.explain: 5 + 10 + 15 = 30. The others make 50 and 45.
quiz.mistake: Does not add all three

quiz.q: Star puzzle: 4 is in the middle and each line must add to 12. Which number goes on the line with 1?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to count the middle 4

quiz.q: Star puzzle: 4 is in the middle and each line adds to 12. Which number goes on the line with 2?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the middle number

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I know whether to put + or - in 12 ___ 5 = 7?
teach.praise: Yes! 7 is smaller than 12, so it must be take away.
teach.nudge: Is the answer bigger or smaller than the first number?

revise.summary: To make a total, try pairs that add up to it. To fill + or -, use + if the answer is bigger than the first number and - if it is smaller.
focus: Find numbers that add to a total.
Choose + or - to make a sum true.
Solve the star puzzle.
remember: Answer bigger than the first number: use +. Smaller: use -.
Star puzzle: 4 in the middle; pair 1 and 7, 2 and 6, 3 and 5. Each line adds to 12.
traps: Don't always pick + or always pick -.
Don't forget the middle 4 in the star puzzle.
Add to check your pairs.

learn.hook: Many roads lead to the park! How many ways can you go?
points: Count routes carefully, one at a time, so you do not miss any.
2 roads from home to the shop and 3 roads from the shop to school make 6 ways from home to school.
In a maze, trace the path with your finger and go back from dead ends.
To split a region equally, every part must get the same number of things.

example.q: 2 roads go from home to the shop. 2 roads go from the shop to school. How many ways from home to school?
steps: Road A, then road X or road Y: 2 ways.
Road B, then road X or road Y: 2 ways.

learn.reallife: Delivery riders choose between many routes in a city.

games.title: True or false?
items: In a maze we should go back from dead ends
A dead end does not lead out, so we try another way.
2 roads to the shop and 1 road on to school make 2 ways in all
Take either road, then the one road.
Equal parts can have different numbers of things
Equal parts must have the same number.
8 trees in 2 equal parts gives 4 trees in each
When counting routes, it is fine to skip some

items.q: 6 trees in 3 equal parts: trees in each
12 flowers in 4 equal parts: in each
Maze path passes 3 apples and 4 mangoes: fruits

quiz.q: 3 roads go from home to the shop. 2 roads go from the shop to school. How many ways from home to school?
quiz.explain: Each of the 3 roads can be followed by 2 roads: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
steps: Road 1: 2 ways, Road 2: 2 ways, Road 3: 2 ways
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 2
