quiz.explain: She must take the one road, then any of the 4 roads. That is 4 ways.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 and 4

quiz.q: In a maze, Ravi's path passes 3 bananas and 2 apples. He picks them all. How many fruits does he get?
quiz.explain: 3 + 2 = 5 fruits.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: In a maze, what should you do at a dead end?
options: Go back and try another way
quiz.explain: A dead end has no way out, so go back and try a different path.
steps: A dead end has no way out.
Answer: Go back and try another way
quiz.mistake: Gives up at a dead end

quiz.q: A garden has 6 trees. The gardener divides it into 3 equal parts. How many trees are in each part?
quiz.explain: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6, so each part has 2 trees.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 3 instead of sharing

quiz.q: A box of 12 crayons is split into 4 equal parts. How many crayons are in each part?
quiz.mistake: Takes away 4 instead of sharing

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I count all the ways to get to school?
teach.praise: Yes! Count every route one by one so none is missed.
teach.nudge: How can I make sure I do not miss a route?

revise.summary: Count routes one at a time so you do not miss any. In a maze, trace the path and go back from dead ends, and to split equally, every part must get the same number.
focus: Count the ways from home to school.
Solve a maze.
Split things into equal parts.
remember: 2 roads to the shop and 3 roads to school make 6 ways.
At a dead end, go back and try another way.
traps: Don't add 3 and 2 for the ways. Each road can be followed by every next road.
Don't take away 3 when sharing into 3 equal parts.

learn.hook: How many cuts to cut a 6 m cloth into 1 m pieces? Not 6!
points: To cut something into pieces, you need 1 cut fewer than the number of pieces.
6 m of cloth into 1 m pieces gives 6 pieces, so 5 cuts.
Joining 4 dots like corners can make a rectangle. A square is a rectangle too.
With 2 rows of 3 dots, you can make 2 small squares and 1 long rectangle: 3 rectangles in all.

example.q: A ribbon is cut into 4 equal pieces. How many cuts?
steps: 2 cuts make 3 pieces. 3 cuts make 4 pieces.

learn.reallife: A tailor cuts cloth, and we cut a cake into pieces at a party.

games.title: True or false?
items: To cut a 6 m cloth into 1 m pieces, you need 6 cuts
One cut splits it into two.
A square is also a rectangle
It has 4 square corners and opposite sides equal.

quiz.q: A 6 m cloth is cut into 1 m pieces. How many cuts are needed?
quiz.explain: 6 pieces need 1 cut fewer: 6 - 1 = 5 cuts.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the cuts equal the pieces

quiz.q: How many pieces do 3 cuts make in a straight ribbon?
quiz.explain: Each cut adds 1 piece. 3 cuts make 3 + 1 = 4 pieces.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the pieces equal the cuts

quiz.q: A log is cut into 8 pieces. How many cuts were made?
quiz.explain: 8 pieces need 8 - 1 = 7 cuts.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the cuts equal the pieces

quiz.q: 4 dots sit like the corners of a square. You join them. How many rectangles do you get?
quiz.explain: Joining the 4 corner dots makes 1 square, and a square is a rectangle.
steps: A square is a rectangle. Answer: 1
quiz.mistake: Thinks a square is not a rectangle

quiz.q: Dots are in 2 rows of 3. Joining dots, how many rectangles can you make, counting squares too?
quiz.explain: 2 small squares and 1 long rectangle: 2 + 1 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the small squares

quiz.q: Dots in 2 rows of 3 make how many small squares?
quiz.explain: Each small square uses 4 dots side by side. There are 2 of them.
steps: Each small square uses 4 dots side by side.
quiz.mistake: Counts the long rectangle as a square

teach.ask: Gappu: How many cuts do I need to make 6 pieces of cloth?
teach.praise: Yes! 5 cuts. You always need 1 cut fewer than the pieces.
teach.nudge: Is it the same number as the pieces, or 1 fewer?

revise.summary: To cut something into pieces, you need 1 cut fewer than the number of pieces. Joining dots can make rectangles, and a square is a rectangle too.
focus: Find the cuts for a number of pieces.
Find the pieces from a number of cuts.
Count rectangles made by joining dots.
remember: Cuts = pieces - 1.
A square is a rectangle too.
2 rows of 3 dots: 2 small squares and 1 long rectangle = 3.
traps: The cuts are not equal to the pieces.
Don't think a square is not a rectangle.
Don't count only the small squares.
